name: Multigenerational Home Renovation Tax Credit
summary: A refundable federal tax credit worth up to $7,000 for 2026 ($7,250 for 2025) for building a self-contained secondary unit so a senior or an adult with a disability can live with a relative.
description:
This credit helps families create a separate, self-contained living space, with its own private entrance, kitchen, bathroom and sleeping area, so that a senior aged 65 or older, or an adult eligible for the disability tax credit, can live with a relative.

You can claim up to $50,000 of qualifying costs for each qualifying renovation. The credit rate follows the lowest federal tax rate: 15% for 2023 and 2024 (up to $7,500), 14.5% for 2025 (up to $7,250) and 14% from 2026 (up to $7,000). Because it is refundable, you can receive it even if you owe no tax.

You claim it for the tax year the renovation is completed. Only one renovation can be claimed for each qualifying individual in their lifetime, and both the senior or adult with a disability and the relative must live in the home within 12 months after the work ends.
incentives: Building a secondary unit for a senior or adult with a disability: 14% of up to $50,000 in costs (2026)
eligibility: The renovation creates a self-contained secondary unit (private entrance, kitchen, bathroom and sleeping area) in a home in Canada | The unit is for a qualifying individual: a senior (65+ at the end of the year) or an adult aged 18 to 64 eligible for the disability tax credit | The qualifying individual and a qualifying relative (18+; for example a parent, child, grandchild, sibling, aunt, uncle, niece or nephew) must live in the home within 12 months after the renovation ends | The home is owned by the qualifying individual or the qualifying relative | Only one renovation can be claimed for each qualifying individual in their lifetime
howToApply: Keep all invoices and proof of payment for the renovation | Calculate the credit on Schedule 12 when you file for the year the renovation was completed | Enter the result on line 45355 of your federal income tax return | Keep supporting documents in case the CRA asks for them
notes: The lowest federal tax rate is 14% for 2026, which sets the 2026 maximum at $7,000. CRA's detailed credit page still describes the 2025 tax year, so check the 2026 version when you file. Some costs may qualify for both this credit and the Home Accessibility Tax Credit. The related Canada Secondary Suite Loan Program was cancelled before it launched.

name: Electric Vehicle Affordability Program
summary: A point-of-sale discount of up to $5,000 on a new battery-electric or fuel-cell vehicle (up to $2,500 for plug-in hybrids), applied by the dealer. Amounts drop starting in 2027.
description:
The Electric Vehicle Affordability Program replaced the old iZEV rebate and applies to new eligible vehicles bought or leased from February 16, 2026 until March 31, 2031, or until funding runs out. The discount is taken off the bill of sale or lease by an enrolled dealer, so you do not apply yourself.

In 2026, battery-electric and hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles get $5,000 and plug-in hybrids get $2,500. The amount steps down each year (to $4,000 and $2,000 in 2027, and down to $2,000 and $1,000 by 2030-2031), and it is based on the date the dealer submits the claim, not your purchase date.

To qualify, the vehicle must be new (or a demo under 10,000 km), made in Canada or in a country with which Canada has a free-trade agreement, and have a final transaction price of $50,000 or less unless it was built in Canada. Leases of 48 months or longer get the full amount; shorter leases of at least 12 months are prorated. Individuals can receive one incentive over the life of the program.
amountDisplay: Up to $5,000 in 2026 (declining in later years)
incentives: Battery-electric or hydrogen fuel-cell vehicle (2026): $5,000 | Plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (2026): $2,500
eligibility: New light-duty vehicle (under 8,500 lb) bought or leased on or after February 16, 2026; demonstrators with under 10,000 km also qualify | Made in Canada or in a country with which Canada has a free-trade agreement | Final transaction value of $50,000 or less, unless the vehicle was made in Canada (no price cap) | Must be highway-capable and meet Canadian motor vehicle safety standards | Leases must be at least 12 months; leases of 48 months or more get the full amount | One incentive per individual over the program; businesses and governments up to 10
howToApply: Check Transport Canada's list of eligible vehicles | Buy or lease from an enrolled dealership or authorized seller | Sign the consumer consent form so the dealer can confirm your eligibility with Transport Canada | Sign the attestation form; the incentive is deducted on the bill of sale or lease after taxes and fees
notes: The amount depends on the date your dealer submits the claim, not the date you buy, so a vehicle bought in late 2026 could get the lower 2027 amount if the claim is filed in January. You cannot apply yourself; the dealer applies the discount and files the claim. The program can end before March 31, 2031 if funding runs out. If the rules are broken or false information is given, Transport Canada can recover the incentive and you agree to repay the dealer. Some provinces offer their own EV rebates; check with the provincial program whether they can be combined.

name: Home Accessibility Tax Credit
summary: A non-refundable federal tax credit on up to $20,000 a year of renovations that make a home safer or more accessible for a senior or a person with a disability, worth up to $2,800 for 2026 ($2,900 for 2025).
description:
The Home Accessibility Tax Credit lets you claim up to $20,000 a year of eligible renovation costs that improve access or mobility in a home, or reduce the risk of harm, for someone aged 65 or older or eligible for the disability tax credit. Examples include walk-in tubs, grab bars, ramps, wider doorways and stairlifts.

The credit is non-refundable and calculated at the lowest federal tax rate, so it can reduce federal tax owing by up to $2,800 for 2026 (14%) or $2,900 for 2025 (14.5%). When more than one qualifying person lives in the home, the $20,000 limit applies to the home as a whole.

Routine repairs and maintenance, appliances, home-entertainment electronics, housekeeping, gardening, security monitoring, financing costs and renovations done mainly to raise the property's value do not qualify. Work or goods from a related person count only if that person is registered for GST/HST.
amountDisplay: Credit on up to $20,000 a year of costs (up to $2,800 for 2026; $2,900 for 2025)
incentives: Accessibility or safety renovations: Lowest federal rate on up to $20,000 a year
eligibility: The qualifying individual is 65 or older at the end of the year, or eligible for the disability tax credit | The qualifying individual, or an eligible family member, can claim | The home is in Canada and is owned and ordinarily lived in by the qualifying individual, or is an eligible family member's home where the qualifying individual lives | The renovation is of an enduring nature and improves access, mobility or safety | Your own labour and tools are not eligible
howToApply: Keep receipts and invoices for the work | Complete the line 31285 chart on the Federal Worksheet (5000-D1) | Enter the amount on line 31285 of your federal return | Do not send receipts with your return, but keep them for CRA review
notes: The CRA sets the $20,000 annual expense limit; the dollar maximums shown are that limit multiplied by the lowest federal tax rate (14% for 2026, 14.5% for 2025). If both your taxable income and your total non-refundable credits are above the first federal bracket ($58,523 for 2026), a temporary top-up credit keeps the rate at 15% on the part above that threshold. Some provinces offer their own accessibility credits.

name: Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program
administrator: Natural Resources Canada (transitioning to Environment and Climate Change Canada), delivered by provincial partners
categories: heat-pumps | insulation | air-sealing | windows-doors | smart-thermostats | solar | low-income
summary: Federally funded, no-cost home energy upgrades for low- and median-income homeowners and tenants. You apply through your province's or utility's partner program, not through Ottawa.
description:
The Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program is the federal successor to the Greener Homes Grant for lower-income households. Instead of reimbursing homeowners, it pays for upgrades directly: a partner organization plans and installs the work, and eligible participants pay nothing out of pocket.

For the first time in a federal retrofit program, tenants who pay their own energy bills can take part, not only owners. Typical upgrades include insulation, air sealing and heat pumps, and in some regions windows, doors or smart thermostats. The exact list depends on the provincial partner.

As of October 2026 the program is delivered by BC Hydro and FortisBC in British Columbia, Efficiency Manitoba's Energy Efficiency Assistance Program, Efficiency Nova Scotia's HomeWarming and African Nova Scotian Communities Retrofit programs, Prince Edward Island's home insulation programs, and Hydro-Québec's offers for modest-income households. No territory and no other province has a partner program yet; the federal government says more will be added.
amountDisplay: Upgrades at no cost to eligible households
incentives: Insulation and air sealing: Covered in full | Heat pumps: Covered in full | Windows, doors, smart thermostats: Covered in full where offered
eligibility: Low- to median-income households (thresholds set by each provincial partner) | Homeowners, and tenants who pay their own energy bills | Must live in a province with an active delivery partner (currently BC, MB, NS, PE and QC) | Indigenous governments and organizations receive funding through separate federal agreements
howToApply: Find the partner program for your province on the federal program page | Apply directly to that partner (BC Hydro, FortisBC, Efficiency Manitoba, Efficiency Nova Scotia, the PEI home insulation programs or Hydro-Québec) | Complete the partner's income verification and home assessment | The partner arranges and pays for the installation
notes: The federal government does not take applications from households; you apply through the partner program in your province. As of October 2026 there is no partner program in Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador or the territories. In Ontario, income-qualified households can apply to Save on Energy's Energy Affordability Program and Enbridge's Home Winterproofing Program. Natural Resources Canada says it has not authorized any company to contact homeowners unsolicited about this program, so be cautious of calls, emails or door-to-door offers.

name: CMHC Eco Plus
summary: A 25% refund of your CMHC mortgage insurance premium when you buy a newly built, energy-efficient home with a CMHC-insured mortgage.
description:
If you buy a never-occupied, energy-efficient home (including a new condo unit or a prefabricated home) with a CMHC-insured mortgage, you can ask CMHC to refund 25% of your mortgage loan insurance premium.

The home needs either an eligible certification (such as ENERGY STAR, R-2000, LEED, CHBA Net Zero, Built Green, Novoclimat, Passive House or certain BC Energy Step Code levels) or an EnerGuide rating at least 20% better than a typical new home.

You must apply within two years of your mortgage closing. On a typical insured mortgage the refund can amount to a few thousand dollars, depending on the size of the premium.

incentives: Newly built energy-efficient home with CMHC-insured mortgage: 25% of the insurance premium

notes: This refund only applies to mortgages insured by CMHC; ask your lender which insurer was used. CMHC's current rules cover newly built homes only, so renovating an existing home does not qualify. Apply within two years of your mortgage closing. Owners of rental buildings should look instead at the CMHC multi-unit mortgage insurance product for retrofits that was announced in October 2026.

name: Home Renovation Program
summary: Nunavummiut who own and live in their homes can get a forgivable loan of up to $100,000 for major repairs and renovations, including energy efficiency work, or a 50% rebate up to $20,000 for completed repairs.
description:
The Home Renovation Program funds major repairs and renovations to owner-occupied homes. Projects are ranked by priority: health and safety first, then overcrowding, then energy efficiency (building envelope, windows and doors, heating, electrical and plumbing systems), then weather resistance and durability.

The forgivable loan covers materials, freight and labour, and the amount depends on household income: up to $100,000 for incomes up to $125,000, $80,000 up to $150,000, $60,000 up to $175,000 and $40,000 up to the Average Income Required for Homeownership. Nothing is forgiven in the first five years; 20% is forgiven on each anniversary in years six to ten, as long as you keep living in the home.

There is also a rebate stream that pays 50% of eligible completed repairs, up to $20,000 over your lifetime, which is available to households above the income limit. Heating oil tank replacements, once a separate program, are now handled under the HRP, and it can be combined with the Emergency Repair Program.
amountDisplay: Forgivable loan up to $100,000, or rebate up to $20,000
incentives: Renovations and repairs (forgivable loan): $40,000 to $100,000 depending on income | Completed repairs (rebate stream): 50% up to $20,000 lifetime | Heating oil tank replacement: Covered under the HRP
eligibility: At least 19 years old and living in Nunavut for at least two years | Own (title or leasehold title) and live in the home as your principal residence | Home at least five years old, within a Nunavut municipal boundary and connected to the QEC grid | For the forgivable loan, household income below the Average Income Required for Homeownership

notes: If you sell the home or stop living in it during the 10-year term, the remaining loan balance becomes payable. NHC registers its interest on your property while the loan is outstanding.

name: Better Buildings Program
administrator: Government of Yukon, Energy Branch (Energy, Mines and Resources) with participating municipalities
summary: Yukon property owners can borrow up to $50,000 for home energy retrofits at a rate tied to the Bank of Canada rate and repay it through a local improvement charge on their property taxes.
description:
The Better Buildings Program lends money for upgrades that reduce annual energy use, such as insulation, air sealing and heat pumps. Residential loans are capped at $50,000 and at 25% of the property's assessed value, with a one-time $500 administration fee. Commercial buildings can borrow up to $100,000.

Repayment is added to annual property taxes as a local improvement charge. Owners in participating municipalities and on rural properties outside municipal boundaries can apply.
incentives: Residential energy retrofit loan: Up to $50,000
eligibility: Own property in a participating Yukon municipality or in rural Yukon | Upgrades must reduce annual energy consumption
howToApply: Contact the Energy Branch (energy@yukon.ca, 867-393-7063) or apply through the Better Buildings Program page on yukon.ca | Complete the approved retrofit; repayments are added to your property tax bill
notes: The interest rate follows the Bank of Canada rate, so ask for the current rate when you apply. Confirm that your municipality participates before planning your project.

name: Rénoclimat
administrator: Government of Québec (Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs)
summary: Québec's home renovation grant was overhauled on October 1, 2026. It now pays fixed rates for insulation, windows and fixed home batteries without a mandatory energy evaluation, and adds a new flood-adaptation stream.
description:
Since October 1, 2026, Rénoclimat's energy-efficiency stream is a simplified track. The energy evaluation is now optional, with up to $500 to cover it, and the post-work evaluation has been dropped. Grants are paid per square foot or per window up to a cap for each measure: roof insulation at $1.75 per sq ft, exterior wall insulation at $3.50 per sq ft, foundation and floor insulation at $0.50 to $3.50 per sq ft, and ENERGY STAR Most Efficient windows at $300 per opening. Two resilience measures are new: up to $1,000 for a master electrician to connect a backup power source, and up to $4,000 for a fixed home battery. Duplexes, triplexes and buildings of 4 or more units get higher caps. The total for energy work is capped at $21,500 for a house and $31,000 for a duplex, triplex or multi-unit building.

Work must be done on or after October 1, 2026 by a contractor with the matching RBQ licences, who must fill in and sign the program's certificate of compliance. Work you do yourself does not qualify. You apply after the work, within 12 months of finishing it, through a new online portal that Québec says will open during fall 2026.

The new Rénoclimat – Adaptation stream helps principal residences and multi-unit buildings prepare for flooding. Its simplified track covers a sump pump with battery backup, a backflow valve and a removable flood barrier. Its accompanied track, for homes in recognized river-flood zones, starts with a mandatory climate-resilience diagnostic and covers recommended work at 75% of costs up to $35,000. The Adaptation stream is capped at $38,500 per home. This version of the program runs until March 31, 2029, or until its budget runs out.
amountDisplay: Up to $21,500 (house) or $31,000 (duplex, triplex, multi-unit) for energy work, plus up to $38,500 for flood adaptation

If your home already had a pre-work evaluation under the old rules, or you requested one by October 12, 2026, you can finish under the old rules as long as the post-work evaluation is done by March 31, 2027. Heat pumps, doors, air sealing and ventilation are no longer covered; use LogisVert for heat pumps. Rénoclimat cannot be combined with other Québec, federal or municipal aid (including tax credits) for the same work. You can still use LogisVert or a city program for different work on the same home, such as a LogisVert heat pump alongside Rénoclimat wall insulation. The federal Canada Greener Homes Grant and Loan, formerly paired with Rénoclimat, are closed.

name: Elders Housing Program
summary: Nunavut homeowners aged 60 or older, or receiving a disability benefit, can get an annual grant of up to $5,000 for preventative maintenance and a one-time grant of up to $30,000 for repairs and aging-in-place changes.
description:
The Elders Housing Program provides counselling and grants to help Elders and people with disabilities stay in their homes. The annual preventative maintenance grant (up to $5,000) covers upkeep of heating, plumbing, electrical systems and appliances. The one-time grant (up to $30,000) covers accessibility changes such as ramps, stair lifts and bathroom modifications, equipment requested by medical professionals, and other repairs that improve living conditions.

There is no maximum income, but applications are point-rated, with more weight given to lower-income households. The program can be combined with the Home Renovation Program.

name: Renewable Energy Homeowners Grant
administrator: Government of Nunavut, Department of Environment (Climate Change Secretariat) with Nunavut Housing Corporation
summary: Homeowners within Nunavut municipal boundaries have been able to recover half the cost of a solar or wind system, up to $30,000, after it is approved for Qulliq Energy's net metering program.
description:
The grant, created in 2021, pays 50% of the cost of a home renewable electricity system up to $30,000. Applicants pay upfront and are reimbursed after submitting receipts. The Government of Nunavut's Sustainable Energy Support Policy, which replaced the 2021 policy, says support for homeowner energy programs continues.

The home must first be approved for Qulliq Energy Corporation's net metering program, which accepts residential systems of up to 15 kW (AC). Qulliq Energy recommends not buying a system until your net metering application has been reviewed and approved.

name: Renewable Energy Rebates
administrator: Arctic Energy Alliance (funded by the Government of the Northwest Territories)
summary: NWT residents can get up to $20,000 for solar and other renewable energy systems, or up to $30,000 for biomass heating such as wood-pellet boilers, with pre-approval and while funds last.
description:
AEA pays the lowest of 50% of eligible costs, a savings-based calculation (for systems other than solar electric) or, for solar electric, $4.00 per watt of capacity. Residents can receive up to $30,000 for biomass heating and up to $20,000 for other projects; most businesses and non-profits can receive up to $50,000.

Eligible technologies include solar PV, wind and micro-hydro, solar water and air heating, and wood pellet and EPA-certified wood boilers and furnaces. Grid-connected renewable electricity is no longer eligible in hydro-powered communities, where residents can use the utility's net metering instead; off-grid projects there still qualify. Batteries are eligible for stand-alone systems and grid-tied systems with battery backup, but not as replacements.

Projects need pre-approval, must be finished within four months of approval, and final paid invoices are due within one month of completion.

name: CleanBC Energy Savings Program (ground-oriented homes)
administrator: Province of B.C. (CleanBC Better Homes), delivered by CLEAResult
summary: Income-tested rebates, paid directly to registered contractors, that cover up to the full cost of a heat pump or heat pump water heater for lower- and middle-income B.C. households.
description:
The Energy Savings Program is B.C.'s income-qualified rebate program for detached houses, row homes and other ground-oriented housing. You pre-register with proof of income, get an eligibility code, and a registered contractor takes the rebate off your invoice, so you only pay the balance. Most rebates cover 100% of eligible costs up to the maximum for your income level.

The biggest rebates are for switching from oil, natural gas or propane: up to $13,000 for a central ducted or three-head heat pump at Level 1, $7,000 at Level 2 and $3,500 at Level 3, or up to $16,500 / $11,500 / $7,000 for a combined space and water heating heat pump. Homes heated with electricity can get up to $5,000 at Level 1 only, and wood-heated homes up to $5,000 (Level 1) or $4,000 (Level 2).

Heat pump water heaters earn up to $3,500. Add-ons cover electrical service upgrades for fossil-fuel switches (up to $5,000), ventilation, and health and safety repairs, and northern homes switching from fossil fuels get a top-up of up to $3,000.

The program changed for invoices dated on or after July 6, 2026: insulation and window rebates were removed, fossil-fuel heat pump amounts were reduced, and Level 2 households with electric heat no longer qualify for a heat pump rebate.

name: Dependable Grid Program
administrator: Government of Yukon, Energy Branch (Energy, Mines and Resources)
summary: Yukon rebates of up to $15,000 for electrically heated and new homes that add a dual-fuel heat pump system, a non-electric backup or primary heater, non-electric hot water or a generator transfer switch, to cut winter peak electricity demand.
description:
The Dependable Grid Program opened on April 15, 2026 to reduce demand on Yukon's isolated grid during cold snaps. It is aimed at homes already heated with electricity and new homes under construction, and was funded mostly by money moved from the cancelled electric transportation rebates.

A dual-fuel system (a heat pump plus a non-electric backup) or a switch to a non-electric primary heating system can receive 50% of costs up to $15,000 in an existing home, or a flat $15,000 in a new home. A secondary wood stove, pellet stove, oil monitor or propane fireplace is covered at 50% up to $5,000 in existing homes, or a flat $3,000 in new homes. New homes built to very high efficiency get $12,500 for Tier 5 or $2,000 for Tier 4. The program also pays $100 per smart vehicle outlet that moves workplace block-heater use off peak, and offers sign-up bonuses and annual rewards for joining Yukon Energy's Peak Smart Home program or charging an EV off peak.

summary: Ontario's main home-retrofit rebate program. You can claim single upgrades such as a heat pump, attic insulation, solar with a battery, a smart thermostat or ENERGY STAR appliances without an energy assessment, or do an assessment and two or more upgrades for envelope rebates.
description:
Home Renovation Savings is run jointly by Save on Energy and Enbridge Gas, with support from the Ontario government. It started on January 28, 2025, replacing Enbridge's Home Efficiency Rebate, and has two tracks.

In the no-assessment track you claim one or more single upgrades: cold-climate air-source or ground-source heat pumps, attic insulation, rooftop solar with optional battery storage, smart thermostats and ENERGY STAR Most Efficient appliances. Heat pumps and attic insulation go through a participating contractor, and heat pumps need pre-approval before installation.

In the assessment track a registered energy advisor does a first assessment, you complete at least two recommended upgrades, and the advisor does a follow-up assessment. This track covers attic, wall, foundation, crawlspace and exposed-floor insulation, windows and doors, air sealing and heat pump water heaters, and refunds $600 of the assessment costs. Completing three or more upgrades adds a $500 bonus. Total assessment-track rebates are capped at $5,000 for homes heated by Enbridge natural gas and $10,000 for homes heated by electricity, oil, propane or wood.

Heat pump rebates depend on how the home is heated now. Homes heated by electricity, oil, propane or wood get the highest per-ton amounts. Homes heated by Enbridge natural gas, and heat pumps that are rented rather than bought, get lower amounts.

The solar and battery rebates cover rooftop systems built for load displacement only, so you cannot also sign a net-metering agreement, and a battery must be installed with new solar. You need written pre-approval before buying or installing solar or storage equipment.

Applications go through the Good Energy Rebates portal after installation, with itemized receipts that show a zero balance. Payment can take up to 12 weeks.

name: Renewable Energy Cabin Grant
administrator: Government of Nunavut, Department of Environment (Climate Change Secretariat)
summary: Nunavut residents who own a cabin can get a one-time grant of up to $5,000 to install a solar or wind system, with batteries, at the cabin.
description:
The Climate Change Secretariat gives cabin owners a one-time, non-repayable grant of up to $5,000 per cabin for CSA-certified solar PV or wind systems and the batteries that support them, including shipping of the equipment. Labour is not an eligible cost.

You must be approved before buying or installing anything, then finish the project within 12 months of approval and send receipts and photos of the installation. The grant is paid about four weeks after the completed paperwork is received.

A fixed amount of funding is available each year and is given out first come, first served, so it can run out before year end.
incentives: Cabin solar or wind system with supporting batteries: Up to $5,000, one time per cabin
eligibility: Nunavut resident (primary residence in Nunavut), 19 or older, who owns the cabin (signed statutory declaration) | Cabin is a permanent structure in a remote location used for camping or traditional land use, not a primary residence | One grant per cabin; approval required before purchase and installation
howToApply: Email renewableenergy@gov.nu.ca to confirm your project qualifies | Get quotes, then submit the cabin grant application form by email, mail or in person | After approval, install within 12 months and send receipts and photos
notes: The Climate Change Secretariat replies in writing within 30 days of receiving a complete application. Apply early in the year, as funding is limited.

name: Manitoba Electric Vehicle Rebate Program
administrator: Government of Manitoba, delivered by Manitoba Public Insurance
summary: Manitoba pays $4,000 toward a new electric vehicle and $2,500 toward a used one bought or leased from a Manitoba dealer; the program was extended in Budget 2026.
description:
The Manitoba EV rebate gives $4,000 for a new eligible battery-electric or plug-in hybrid vehicle and $2,500 for a used one. Leases of at least 12 months qualify on a sliding scale: $1,000 to $4,000 for new vehicles and $625 to $2,500 for used vehicles, depending on lease length. New vehicles must have an MSRP under $70,000, and used vehicles a purchase price under $70,000. In 2026 the vehicle must be a 2023 model year or newer (2024 or newer in 2027).

The vehicle must be bought or leased from an authorized Manitoba dealer and stay registered in Manitoba in the owner's name for at least 12 months. Teslas and EVs made in China bought after March 19, 2025 are not eligible, and a used vehicle that already received a rebate cannot get another.

The program first ran from July 1, 2024 to March 31, 2026 and was extended in Manitoba's Budget 2026. Funding is first come, first served. Buyers who receive the federal EV incentive can also apply.
incentives: New EV purchase: $4,000 | Used EV purchase: $2,500 | New EV lease (12+ months): $1,000 to $4,000 | Used EV lease (12+ months): $625 to $2,500
eligibility: Manitoba resident, business, First Nation or municipality (Crown corporations and governments excluded) | Bought or leased from an authorized Manitoba dealer; private sales and out-of-province purchases do not qualify | Model year 2023 or newer in 2026 (2024 or newer in 2027) | Registered in Manitoba in the owner's name for at least 12 months | Not a Tesla or China-built EV bought after March 19, 2025; one rebate per person or organization and per vehicle
howToApply: Buy or lease an eligible EV from a Manitoba dealer and register it in Manitoba | Apply online at evrebate.mpi.mb.ca (no fee) | A cheque is issued about 45 to 60 days after approval
notes: Check the province's eligible vehicle list before you buy, because it can change at any time. The rebate cannot be assigned to the dealer and does not cover home chargers; a Level 2 charger can be financed through Manitoba Hydro's Home Energy Efficiency Loan. Questions: EVRebate@mpi.mb.ca.

name: Novoclimat – Certified Energy-Efficient New Homes
administrator: Government of Québec (Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs)
summary: Buyers of a new home built and certified to the Novoclimat standard get a $2,000 grant, or $4,000 if they are first-time buyers.
description:
Novoclimat certifies new homes built by certified contractors to energy-efficiency standards above the building code. Once a house is certified, the first buyer receives $2,000, or $4,000 for a first-time buyer. The builder separately receives $1,500, or $2,500 at the Novoclimat Sélect level.

The Novoclimat option has to be in the sales contract before construction starts. An evaluator inspects the home during construction, and certification triggers the grant: the owner receives the certificate and a claim form by mail, and a cheque follows within 10 weeks of sending it back. Certified homes may also qualify for CMHC's Eco Plus mortgage-insurance refund and green-mortgage discounts from some lenders. Small multi-unit buildings have their own per-unit grants, paid to the applicant once the building is certified.
incentives: Buyer grant – certified Novoclimat home: $2,000 | First-time buyer grant: $4,000
eligibility: Newly built house (detached, semi-detached, row, two-generation, or with an attached unit) built by a Novoclimat-certified contractor | Novoclimat option included in the sales contract before construction begins | Home must receive Novoclimat certification after inspection | Buyer grant goes to the first buyer
howToApply: Choose a Novoclimat-certified builder and add the Novoclimat option to your purchase contract before construction. | The builder registers the project, and an evaluator inspects during construction. | After certification, fill in the claim form you receive by mail and return it. A cheque follows within 10 weeks.
notes: No end date is published. Small multi-unit Novoclimat buildings receive $500 to $1,700 per unit ($1,000 to $3,400 for social-purpose housing), paid to the applicant rather than to individual buyers. An eligible heat pump in a Novoclimat home may also qualify for LogisVert. Some older bonuses still quoted online, such as low-temperature heat pump bonuses, have ended.

name: Heating Rebates for Biomass, Firewood and Wood Pellets
summary: PEI still offers rebates on qualifying wood and pellet stoves, furnaces and boilers, and a 10% rebate on firewood and wood pellet purchases.
description:
When most residential equipment rebates ended on April 15, 2026, biomass heating equipment was reported to remain eligible. Qualifying EPA- or CSA B415.1-certified wood and pellet stoves, furnaces and boilers receive provincial rebates, with higher amounts for income-qualified households.

Separately, Islanders can claim 10% back on eligible firewood and wood pellet purchases.
amountDisplay: Up to $2,000 ($3,500 income-qualified) on equipment; 10% back on firewood and pellets
incentives: Biomass stove: $1,000 | Biomass stove (income-qualified): $1,800 | Biomass boiler or furnace: $2,000 | Biomass boiler or furnace (income-qualified): $3,500 | Firewood and wood pellet purchases: 10% rebate
eligibility: PEI property registered in your name, with the dwelling occupied at least six months before the upgrade | Equipment installed within the previous 12 months in already-heated space | Income-qualified amounts require household income of $35,000 or less and the home must be your primary residence
howToApply: Complete efficiencyPEI's equipment rebate application and include dated receipts and any electrical Certificate of Compliance | Mail or drop it off at efficiencyPEI or any Access PEI location, or call 1-877-734-6336
notes: Equipment amounts are the last ones published by efficiencyPEI (form valid to March 31, 2026) and may have changed. Confirm current details with efficiencyPEI (1-877-734-6336 or efficiencypei@gov.pe.ca) before you start.

name: Efficiency Manitoba Cold Climate Air Source Heat Pump Rebate
summary: A $2,000 rebate for a centrally ducted or $1,500 for a ductless cold climate air source heat pump added to an existing Manitoba home.
description:
Efficiency Manitoba pays a flat rebate for installing a cold climate air source heat pump in an existing home: $2,000 for a centrally ducted system or $1,500 for a ductless system. The heat pump can supplement electric resistance or natural gas heating, and homes converting from propane or fuel oil also qualify.

A registered Efficiency Manitoba contractor obtains the permits, installs the system and submits the rebate application within 90 days of installation, once the system is paid for. Efficiency Manitoba mails the cheque, and a post-installation inspection may be required.

The heat pump cannot replace an existing heat pump, and new homes and seasonal properties are excluded. Efficiency Manitoba recommends improving insulation and getting a pre-retrofit EnerGuide evaluation first so the system can be sized properly.
incentives: Centrally ducted cold climate air source heat pump: $2,000 | Ductless cold climate air source heat pump: $1,500
eligibility: Existing primary residence in Manitoba (new homes and seasonal homes are not eligible) | Heat pump supplements electric resistance or natural gas heating, or replaces propane or fuel oil | Does not replace an existing heat pump system | Installed by an Efficiency Manitoba registered contractor with the required permits
howToApply: Choose a registered contractor and confirm the model qualifies | The contractor obtains permits and installs the heat pump | After you pay, the contractor submits the rebate application within 90 days of installation | Efficiency Manitoba mails the rebate cheque
notes: If you want financing, apply for Manitoba Hydro's Home Energy Efficiency Loan before any work starts or equipment is bought. Income-qualified homes heated by electricity can get a heat pump free through the Energy Efficiency Assistance Program. The federal National Heat Pump Rebate, expected in 2027, is designed to combine with provincial rebates.

name: Energy-Efficient Products Rebates
administrator: Arctic Energy Alliance (funded by the Government of the Northwest Territories)
summary: NWT residents can claim rebates on wood and pellet stoves, programmable thermostats, drain water heat recovery, ECM pumps, ENERGY STAR washers and ventless dryers, and vehicle plug-in controllers installed in the territory.
description:
Arctic Energy Alliance pays rebates on everyday efficient products for residents, businesses, non-profits and community and Indigenous governments. For the April 2026 to March 2027 fiscal year it raised the maximums for wood and pellet stoves, programmable thermostats and ECM pumps, and set the same amounts for hydro and non-hydro communities (except LED lighting). Products no longer have to be bought in the NWT, but they must be new, bought in Canada and installed in the NWT.

Apply within three months of the purchase date with a paid receipt and proof of NWT residence if the receipt has no address. Households can claim up to two of each product type per year (five for programmable thermostats, ECM pumps and plug-in controllers). In 14 communities, select Northern and NorthMart stores take the LED and clothes washer rebate off at the till.

Rebates are not available for fossil-fuel heating systems, or for LED lighting in hydro communities (Behchokǫ̀, Dettah, Enterprise, Fort Resolution, Fort Smith, Hay River, Kátł'odeeche, Ndilǫ and Yellowknife).
incentives: Wood stove or pellet stove: 50% of purchase price up to $2,000 | Drain water heat recovery: $700 | ECM pump: 50% up to $500 | Programmable thermostat: 50% up to $150 each | Automated vehicle plug-in controller: 50% up to $150 | ENERGY STAR washer / ventless dryer / all-in-one washer-dryer: $200 / $500 / $750 | LED bulbs and tubes (non-hydro communities only): Up to $200 per year

notes: Amounts apply to the 2026-27 fiscal year (April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027) and are paid while funds last. Questions: Arctic Energy Alliance, 867-920-3333 or 1-877-755-5855.

name: Roulez vert – Electric Vehicle Rebate
administrator: Government of Québec (Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs)
summary: Québec's EV purchase and lease rebate is in its last year: up to $2,000 for a new battery-electric vehicle and $1,000 for a used one registered in 2026. The program ends December 31, 2026.
description:
Roulez vert has been reduced every year since 2024 and ends on December 31, 2026. For vehicles registered in 2026, the maximums are $2,000 for a new battery-electric or hydrogen fuel-cell vehicle, $1,000 for a plug-in hybrid with a battery of 15 kWh or more, $500 for a smaller plug-in hybrid (8 to under 15 kWh), $500 for an electric motorcycle, and $1,000 for an eligible used battery-electric or fuel-cell vehicle. Nothing is paid for vehicles registered in 2027.

Only the registration date counts. Ordering or putting down a deposit earlier does not lock in a higher amount. New vehicles must be on the eligible list and have a manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP) under $65,000; option packages and features such as all-wheel drive or a bigger battery are added to the price when checking that limit. Leases of 12 months or more qualify, with 25%, 50%, 75% or 100% of the amount for terms of 12, 24, 36 or 48+ months. Used vehicles must be 1 to 4 model years old and bought from a Québec dealer.

Most buyers get the rebate at the dealership, applied directly to the contract, and you can also apply online yourself. The program was suspended from February 1 to March 31, 2025, and vehicles registered in that window are not eligible. Home charger grants moved to the separate Écorecharge program on March 17, 2026.
incentives: New battery-electric vehicle (registered 2026): Up to $2,000 | New hydrogen fuel-cell vehicle: Up to $2,000 | Plug-in hybrid, battery 15 kWh or more: Up to $1,000 | Plug-in hybrid, battery 8 to under 15 kWh: Up to $500 | Used battery-electric or fuel-cell vehicle: Up to $1,000 | Electric motorcycle: Up to $500 | Business electric pickup (MSRP $65,001–$75,000): Up to $2,000

howToApply: Check that the model is on the eligible vehicle list on Québec.ca. | Ask a participating dealer to apply the rebate directly on the purchase or lease contract, or apply online yourself after the vehicle is registered in your name. | Make sure the vehicle is registered on or before December 31, 2026.
notes: Ends December 31, 2026. The official schedule shows $0 for every vehicle type registered in 2027, so the vehicle must be registered by year-end. Sales taxes are calculated on the price before the rebate is subtracted. Roulez vert can be combined with other government incentives, including the federal EV incentive, as long as total public aid stays at or below 75% of the eligible cost.

name: Instant Rebates
summary: Discounts applied at the checkout at participating Nova Scotia retailers on items such as heat pump water heaters, smart thermostats and heat pump clothes dryers.
description:
Efficiency Nova Scotia funds discounts taken off the price at the checkout, so there are no rebate forms. Discounts apply at participating retailers, and the smart thermostat discount is also available online from one manufacturer.

Current homeowner offers cover ENERGY STAR heat pump water heaters, smart thermostats for electric heating, variable-speed pool pumps, heat pump clothes dryers, and outdoor clotheslines and drying racks. Offers change from time to time.
incentives: ENERGY STAR heat pump water heater: $800 off | Smart thermostat for electric heating: $45 off | ENERGY STAR heat pump clothes dryer: $150 off | ENERGY STAR variable-speed pool pump: $200 off | Outdoor clothesline kit or freestanding outdoor dryer: $5 off
eligibility: Purchase an eligible model from a participating retailer in Nova Scotia
howToApply: Buy an eligible product at a participating retailer; the discount is applied at checkout | Use Efficiency Nova Scotia's retailer map to find participating stores
notes: Eligible models and participating stores change; check Efficiency Nova Scotia's retailer map and eligible-model lists before you shop.

name: Efficiency Manitoba EnerGuide Home Evaluation Rebate
summary: A $400 rebate when Manitoba homeowners complete a pre-retrofit EnerGuide home evaluation and plan at least one upgrade within 12 months.
description:
Efficiency Manitoba pays $400 toward a pre-retrofit EnerGuide evaluation of an existing home. An energy advisor from a registered service organization assesses the home's insulation, air tightness, windows, doors and heating and cooling, then emails a report with recommended upgrades about two to three weeks later.

To qualify, you must own the home (including a rental or cottage), it must have active Manitoba Hydro residential service, be heated from September to May and be at least two years old, and you must plan at least one energy efficiency upgrade within the next 12 months. Apply within 90 days of the evaluation.

Only one pre-retrofit evaluation rebate is paid per address. Post-retrofit evaluations, new homes and seasonal or unoccupied homes are not eligible.
incentives: Pre-retrofit EnerGuide evaluation: $400
eligibility: Owner of the home, rental property or cottage evaluated | Active Manitoba Hydro residential service; home heated September to May and at least two years old | Plan to complete at least one energy efficiency upgrade within 12 months | No previous Efficiency Manitoba rebate for a pre-retrofit evaluation at the same address
howToApply: Book a pre-retrofit EnerGuide evaluation with a service organization that serves existing homes | Receive your reports about two to three weeks after the visit | Apply online with the reports within 90 days of the evaluation (paper applications available on request)
notes: A pre-retrofit evaluation is also needed for the insulation air sealing bonus and for Home Energy Retrofits, so book it before starting any work.

name: Free Product Installation
administrator: Efficiency Nova Scotia (EfficiencyOne) (installed by partners Homesol and Summerhill)
summary: Electrically heated Nova Scotia homes can book a free visit to have a smart thermostat professionally installed, along with other small energy-saving devices where eligible.
description:
Efficiency Nova Scotia offers a free smart thermostat (valued at up to $160), professionally installed at no charge. The installer also shows you how to use it.

During the visit, the installer checks whether the home qualifies for other free devices, such as indoor and outdoor motion sensors, solar-powered outdoor security lights, humidity sensors for bathroom fans, faucet aerators, water-saving showerheads and thermostatic shower valves.

Both homeowners and renters can take part; renters need written permission from their landlord or property manager.
amountDisplay: Free smart thermostat (up to $160 value) plus other free devices
incentives: Smart thermostat, installed: Free (valued up to $160) | Motion sensors, solar security lights, bathroom fan humidity sensors and water-saving devices: Free where eligible

howToApply: Fill out the booking form on the Efficiency Nova Scotia website | An installation partner (Homesol or Summerhill) contacts you to book a time
notes: Homes heated mainly by oil, propane or wood do not qualify for this offer; owners of those homes can look at the Home Energy Assessment and Moderate Income Rebate programs.

name: Peak Perks
summary: Get $75 for enrolling an eligible smart thermostat that controls central air or a heat pump, then $20 for each year you stay enrolled. On a few hot weekday afternoons, your cooling is adjusted slightly.
description:
Peak Perks is Ontario's province-wide demand response program for smart thermostats. On a limited number of peak-demand summer weekday afternoons, the IESO can raise your setpoint by up to 2°C for no more than three hours, sometimes after a short pre-cool. You can override any event from your thermostat or app.

You get a $75 virtual prepaid Mastercard when you enrol, plus $20 for each year you stay enrolled. Incentives are paid for up to three thermostats per home. Renters and condo owners with their own central AC can join. Units on a building's central HVAC system cannot.
incentives: Enrolment incentive per thermostat: $75 | Annual participation incentive: $20 per year
eligibility: Ontario residential electricity customer with central air conditioning (including a heat pump that provides central cooling) controlled by an eligible Wi-Fi smart thermostat from Alarm.com, ecobee, Emerson, Google Nest, Honeywell Home or Trane. | Renters are eligible. Condo and apartment units qualify only if they have their own dedicated air conditioning. | Not enrolled in another Ontario program that automatically adjusts your thermostat (Sarnia Saves thermostat participants are the exception). Hydro One customers choose between Peak Perks and myEnergy Rewards. | Cornwall Electric customers are excluded.
howToApply: Enrol at peakperks.ca or through your thermostat maker's app. | Choose your thermostat provider and accept the program terms. | Watch for an email confirming your enrolment. The $75 card arrives within about 60 days.
notes: The prepaid card is virtual and expires six months after it is issued. Incentives are paid for up to three thermostats per home; a replacement thermostat does not earn a new enrolment payment. Peak Perks is a summer cooling program, and EV chargers and home batteries are not listed as eligible devices.

name: Efficiency Manitoba Smart Thermostat Rebate
summary: A $50 rebate on an ENERGY STAR certified smart thermostat installed in a Manitoba home.
description:
Efficiency Manitoba pays $50 when you buy and install an eligible ENERGY STAR certified smart thermostat, new or certified refurbished, bought in Canada. Install it and apply within 90 days of purchase.

The thermostat must be on Efficiency Manitoba's eligible product list and installed in your or your tenant's primary residence, or a cottage heated year-round. Line-voltage thermostats for baseboard heaters, apartments, seasonal homes and vacation rentals are not eligible.

Owners of a qualifying ecobee thermostat can also enrol in Efficiency Manitoba's Peak Partners program, which makes small adjustments to heating or cooling during peak periods.
incentives: ENERGY STAR smart thermostat: $50
eligibility: ENERGY STAR certified smart thermostat on Efficiency Manitoba's eligible list, new or certified refurbished, bought in Canada | Installed in your or your tenant's primary residence, or a year-round heated cottage | Application and receipt received within 90 days of purchase | Not eligible: line-voltage (baseboard) thermostats, apartments, seasonal homes, vacation rentals, commercial properties
howToApply: Check that your thermostat is on the eligible list and compatible with your heating system | Install it, then apply online with your receipt within 90 days of purchase (paper applications available on request) | Keep the receipt and model number until you are paid, in case Efficiency Manitoba asks for photos
notes: If you plan to replace your furnace or add a heat pump soon, wait to buy the thermostat so it is compatible with the new system. Income-qualified households can get a smart thermostat free through the Energy Efficiency Assistance Program. Efficiency Manitoba also runs seasonal in-store instant rebates of $5 to $10 on selected products from September 10 to December 10.

name: Affordable Home Energy Program: Ground Source Heat Pump Offer
summary: Qualifying Manitoba homeowners can install a ground source (geothermal) heat pump with no upfront cost and repay a fixed, interest-free $75 a month for 15 years ($13,500 in total) on their energy bill.
description:
Under the Affordable Home Energy Program's homeowner offer, Efficiency Manitoba covers the upfront cost of a ground source heat pump and pays the contractor directly. The homeowner repays $75 a month, interest-free, for 15 years ($13,500 in total) on the Manitoba Hydro energy bill.

Retrofit projects costing more than $38,000, and replacements of an existing ground source system costing more than $18,500, need an upfront contribution from the homeowner, as can any related upgrades the home needs. The repayment becomes due in full if the home is sold or changes ownership; it does not transfer to the buyer.

Retrofits must replace an electric furnace or boiler, electric baseboards or natural gas heating; homes converting from fuel oil also qualify for incentives. New homes and replacement ground source systems are eligible. Income-qualified households can get a ground source heat pump free through the Energy Efficiency Assistance Program.
amountDisplay: No upfront cost; $75/month for 15 years, interest-free
incentives: Ground source heat pump, homeowner offer: No upfront cost, then $75/month interest-free for 15 years

howToApply: Choose a registered ground source contractor, who applies on your behalf | Wait for Efficiency Manitoba's approval email before any work starts; you then have one year to install | Sign the completion declaration with your contractor; Efficiency Manitoba pays the contractor | The $75 monthly payment is added to your Manitoba Hydro energy bill
notes: If you plan to sell within 15 years, remember the remaining balance must be paid off at sale. Improving insulation first can reduce the size and cost of the system. Ground source heat pumps are the one upgrade that Home Energy Retrofits allows you to combine with this offer.

name: African Nova Scotian Communities Retrofit Program

summary: African Nova Scotian homeowners in Preston Township and Guysborough-area communities can get a free home energy assessment, and low- to moderate-income households can receive upgrades such as insulation, weatherproofing and a switch from oil to a heat pump, usually at no cost.
description:
Efficiency Nova Scotia launched this program in late 2024 as a pilot in two communities with deep African Nova Scotian roots: Preston Township (North Preston, East Preston, Cherry Brook and Lake Loon) and the Guysborough area (Sunnyville, Lincolnville, Upper Big Tracadie, Monastery and Mulgrave).

Eligible homeowners above the income limits may still receive a free home energy assessment, expert advice and installation of energy-efficient products. Households within the low- to moderate-income limits can also get insulation and weatherproofing, a switch from oil heating to a heat pump and other upgrades. The program is typically free for eligible participants, although some costs may apply for certain upgrades and income levels.

In 2026 the program received extra federal and provincial money under the Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program; eligibility rules did not change.

name: Efficiency Manitoba Energy Efficiency Assistance Program
administrator: Efficiency Manitoba (co-funded through the federal Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program)
categories: insulation | heat-pumps | heating-systems | windows-doors | smart-thermostats | energy-audits | low-income
summary: Free insulation, free heat pumps for electrically heated homes, low-cost furnace upgrades and other help for income-qualified Manitoba homeowners and renters.
description:
The Energy Efficiency Assistance Program gives income-qualified households a free home energy assessment and pays registered contractors directly for upgrades, so participants pay nothing upfront. Free measures include attic, wall and basement insulation, an ENERGY STAR smart thermostat, energy-saving products such as LED bulbs and low-flow showerheads, and an air source or ground source heat pump for homes heated by an electric furnace, electric baseboards or an electric boiler.

Other offers include a natural gas furnace upgrade for $9.50 a month (replacing a standard-efficiency furnace) or $25 a month (replacing a mid-efficiency furnace) for five years, a $5,000 rebate for upgrading to a high-efficiency natural gas boiler, and $300 for each ENERGY STAR triple-pane window or door.

Renters can take part through their landlord: the landlord applies and each tenant completes a consent form and provides income documents. Red River Métis Citizens apply through Efficiency Manitoba's Métis Energy Efficiency Offers, and apartment buildings through the In-Suite Energy Efficiency Program.

description:

summary: Income-qualified Ontario electricity customers can get free energy upgrades. These range from free saving kits to a full home visit that can include new appliances, insulation, draft-proofing and, for electric or oil-heated homes, a cold-climate heat pump.

The Energy Affordability Program pays the full cost of energy upgrades for lower-income households. It has two levels. Comprehensive Support starts with a free in-home assessment. Homes with electric water heating can get efficient showerheads and aerators, and homes heated by electricity or oil may also get attic or basement insulation, draft-proofing, a smart thermostat and a cold-climate air-source heat pump.

Energy Saving Kits are free do-it-yourself packages mailed to households with somewhat higher incomes. They contain items such as LED bulbs, weatherstripping, a handheld showerhead, aerators and a block heater timer.

Income limits apply, but you can also qualify through benefits such as OESP, LEAP, Ontario Works, ODSP or the Guaranteed Income Supplement, by living in eligible social housing, or by living on reserve. Renters can take part. With federal Oil to Heat Pump Affordability funding, eligible oil-heated homes can get a heat pump at no cost.

name: LogisVert Efficient Homes Program
summary: Hydro-Québec's main home-efficiency program pays grants for heat pumps, geothermal systems, electric thermal storage, roof insulation with air sealing, and a few efficient appliances.
description:
LogisVert is Hydro-Québec's flagship residential efficiency program. The largest grants go to air-source heat pumps, paid per 1,000 BTU/h of heating capacity at -8°C: $50 for an ENERGY STAR unit and $120 for an ENERGY STAR Cold Climate unit. Hydro-Québec advertises up to $6,700 for a heat pump. The heat pump must be new, ENERGY STAR certified, have an outdoor unit of at least 12,000 BTU/h, and be installed in a home whose main heating is electric.

Other measures include $1,500 for bringing a house's roof to at least R-50 and caulking every listed air-leak point, $750 per 1,000 BTU/h for a new geothermal system, $250 per 1,000 BTU/h for replacing an end-of-life geothermal unit (capped at $18,000 for an individual home), and $15,000 to $22,000 for an electric thermal storage (ETS) central system, with or without a central heat pump. For new geothermal and ETS systems, the authorized installer deducts the grant from the invoice, so there is no application to file. There are also $250 grants for an induction range and a heat-pump dryer, which tenants can claim, and $125 to $300 for an efficient pool pump until November 30, 2026.

Claiming two or more measures in one application adds 5% to the total grant. Since June 15, 2026, owners of older rental buildings in areas Hydro-Québec designates as energy insecure can get an extra $100 per 1,000 BTU/h on Cold Climate wall-mounted heat pumps, for a total of $220. The two bonuses cannot be combined. On the Îles-de-la-Madeleine, Cold Climate heat pumps receive $200 per 1,000 BTU/h.

name: Manitoba Hydro Home Energy Efficiency Loan

summary: On-bill financing from Manitoba Hydro of up to $12,500 per home, or up to $20,000 when it includes a ground source heat pump or solar, at 6.20% for the first five years.
description:
Manitoba Hydro lends homeowners money for qualifying energy upgrades and adds the payments to the monthly energy bill. There is no down payment, and Manitoba Hydro pays the contractor or retailer directly. The rate is 6.20% (on approved credit) for the first five years; after that the rate is based on market rates.

Total borrowing is capped at $12,500 per home. Ground source heat pumps and solar PV systems can be financed up to $20,000 over 15 years, and all loans on a home cannot exceed $20,000 combined. Other limits include $10,000 for cold climate air source heat pumps (15 years), $7,500 for natural gas furnaces and boilers (15 years), $7,500 each for insulation, air sealing, windows and doors, water heating, space heating and ventilation (5 years), $5,000 for central air, conventional air source heat pumps, electrical upgrades and radon mitigation, and $3,000 for a Level 2 EV charger.

Applications must be approved before any work starts or materials are bought. Efficiency Manitoba rebates can be combined with the loan.

name: New Home Energy Savings Program
summary: People building a new home in New Brunswick can have their plans energy-modelled for $99 plus HST and receive up to $15,000 depending on how efficient the finished house is.
description:
Builders or owners register before applying for a building permit, pay a $99 plus HST fee, and have their plans modelled by a certified energy advisor, usually within three to four weeks. Construction must be finished within 12 months of registration unless NB Power agrees to more time.

An on-site evaluation of the finished home sets the incentive. Under the performance option, homes over 300 m³ earn $750, $6,250 or $15,000 at tiers 3 to 5, and smaller homes earn $500, $2,500 or $6,500. Under the prescriptive option, owners choose at least five listed upgrades, up to $15,000. A project receives whichever option pays more; the two cannot be combined. Criteria were updated on June 5, 2025 to reflect higher building code standards.

name: Home Renovation Rebate Program
administrator: BC Hydro and FortisBC, with funding from the Province of B.C. (CleanBC)
summary: Rebates for B.C. households of any income for heat pumps in electrically heated homes, insulation, windows and doors, and heat pump water heaters, plus larger heat pump rebates for northern homes leaving oil, gas or propane.
description:
The Home Renovation Rebate Program is B.C.'s main retrofit rebate open to every income level. BC Hydro and FortisBC run it with provincial CleanBC funding, and it covers detached houses, duplexes, row homes, townhomes, mobile homes on a foundation and small multiplexes. Condos and apartments use a separate program.

A heat pump that replaces hard-wired electric heat (baseboards, radiant or an electric furnace) earns $4,000 if it heats the whole home or $1,500 if it heats at least half of it. Insulation pays by area and R-value added, up to $5,500 in total. Windows and doors pay $100 each, up to $2,000, and an electric-to-heat-pump water heater upgrade pays $1,000. Insulation and window rebates are also open to homes heated by FortisBC gas, Pacific Northern Gas, propane or oil.

Homes in northern B.C. (100 Mile House and north) on BC Hydro electricity can get up to $6,000 for a heat pump that replaces oil, gas or propane heat, $4,500 for a dual-fuel ducted heat pump, and $1,000 for a heat pump water heater that replaces a fossil-fuel tank.

Doing two upgrades adds a $300 bonus; doing three or more with before-and-after EnerGuide evaluations can earn $750 to $2,000 instead. Heat pumps and insulation must be installed by a Home Performance Contractor Network (HPCN) member. You pay the contractor and apply for the rebate afterwards.

FortisBC offers larger heat pump rebates to income-qualified customers in its electric service area and to customers of the Grand Forks, Penticton, Summerland and Nelson Hydro municipal utilities. The home must be heated mainly by hard-wired electric heat (baseboards, radiant or an electric furnace), and any backup heat cannot use gas, oil or propane.

A cold-climate centrally ducted system heating the whole home earns up to $12,000, a whole-home mini-split or multi-split up to $9,000, and a partial-home system up to $5,000. Adding one more eligible home renovation upgrade earns a $350 bonus.

name: Énergir Dual-Energy Grants (heat pump added to a natural gas system)
administrator: Énergir, with Hydro-Québec and the Government of Québec
summary: Énergir natural gas customers who switch to Hydro-Québec's dual-energy rate for at least 10 years can get up to $7,300 for adding a heat pump to a gas forced-air system, or up to $11,900 for adding an electric boiler and an electrical upgrade to a gas hot-water system (single-family home or condo).
description:
Dual energy keeps your natural gas system as backup and lets an electric heat pump do most of the heating. Gas takes over only below about -12°C or -15°C, depending on the region. Énergir, Hydro-Québec and the Government of Québec fund grants for homes that switch to Hydro-Québec's dual-energy Rate DT (or a participating municipal or co-op dual-energy rate).

For a gas furnace (forced air), the grant for adding an electric heat pump is up to $7,300 for a single-family home or condo. For a gas boiler (hot water), adding an electric boiler and an electrical upgrade can bring up to $11,900 for a single-family home or condo: up to $4,100 for the boiler and up to $7,800 for the electrical upgrade, which must increase the home's amperage. Duplexes and triplexes get higher amounts. Amounts depend on the size of the equipment and the work needed, and grants cannot exceed 80% of the eligible extra cost; required electrical work can be counted in that cost. With an Énergir Partner contractor, the grant is usually taken off the price of the work.

name: BC Hydro Solar and Battery Rebates (Residential)
summary: Rebates of up to $5,000 for rooftop solar and up to $5,000 for a home battery enrolled in BC Hydro's Peak Saver program.
description:
BC Hydro pays residential customers $1,000 per kW of installed solar, up to $5,000 and no more than half the installed cost. Batteries earn $500 per kWh of storage, also capped at half the cost: up to $1,500 when installed with solar, or up to $5,000 when the battery is enrolled in Peak Saver, BC Hydro's demand-response program. A battery without solar only qualifies if it is enrolled in Peak Saver.

You must submit a self-generation application and receive BC Hydro's technical acceptance before installing, and the system must be designed and installed by a Home Performance Contractor Network member. Solar rebate recipients take service on BC Hydro's self-generation rate (Rate Schedule 2289), which replaced the previous rate on July 1, 2026.

Rebates are paid to the property owner after the system is approved for connection, usually within 60 days. Funding is first-come, first-served.

name: Zero30 Heat Pump Rental Program
summary: Saint John Energy rents ductless mini-split heat pumps with no upfront cost, from $55.36 a month for Saint John Energy customers, including installation, inspections, repairs and replacement. Customers with a good payment history can instead finance a heat pump of their choice, up to $10,000 over seven years.
description:
Saint John Energy, the City of Saint John's own electric utility, rents ductless mini-split heat pumps through its Zero30 program. You book a free 30 to 40 minute home assessment, and the utility installs the unit through its partner Greenfoot Energy Solutions. The monthly rental covers standard installation, periodic inspection, service calls and replacement. Saint John Energy keeps ownership of the unit, and there is no buyout option.

Rates for Saint John Energy customers start at $55.36 a month for a 9,000 BTU wall unit, $55.93 for 12,000 BTU and $56.50 for 15,000 BTU, with floor models and a 24,000 BTU unit costing more. For a limited time, refurbished units are offered at $10 a month off the regular price. Rental rates rose 2.0% on September 1, 2026.

If you would rather own the equipment, Saint John Energy says customers with a good payment history and credit score can buy a heat pump from the vendor of their choice and have the utility finance it, up to $10,000 over seven years. The rental models carried by the program (Panasonic, Fujitsu and LG) qualify for NB Power's Total Home Energy Savings Program rebates.

name: SaskEnergy Homes Beyond Code: Homeowner Rebate
summary: Buyers of a new Saskatchewan home built to Tier 3, 4 or 5 of the National Building Code energy requirements can get a SaskEnergy rebate of $3,000, $5,000 or $9,000.
description:
Homes Beyond Code rewards new homes built to perform better than the minimum energy code. An energy advisor models the home, completes an as-built EnerGuide assessment with a blower door test, and confirms the tier it reaches under section 9.36 of the National Building Code.

Homeowners of qualifying homes receive $3,000 for Tier 3 (20% more efficient than Tier 1), $5,000 for Tier 4 (40% more efficient) or $9,000 for Tier 5 (70% more efficient and net zero energy ready). Tiers 1 and 2 do not qualify. A separate rebate is paid to the builder.

The builder's application must be approved first; the homeowner then applies within 120 days of natural gas service being transferred into their name, and SaskEnergy mails the cheque in about six to eight weeks.
