name: BC Hydro Condo and Apartment Rebate Program
summary: Rebates of up to $2,250 for an in-suite heat pump and $1,000 for a heat pump water heater in electrically heated condos, apartments and stacked townhomes, with no income test.
description:
This BC Hydro program covers individual suites in multi-unit buildings, which the Home Renovation Rebate Program excludes. It only funds electric-to-electric upgrades: replacing hard-wired electric heat with a cold-climate heat pump, or an electric water heater with a heat pump water heater.

A single-head ductless mini-split earns $1,000, and a ductless multi-split earns $750 per indoor head for up to three heads ($2,250). A heat pump water heater earns $1,000. One heat pump rebate and one water heater rebate are allowed per suite.

You must get a pre-approval code from BC Hydro before buying or installing anything, and strata or co-op approval is required. Heat pumps must be installed by a Home Performance Contractor Network member. Suite owners and owners of purpose-built rental buildings can apply; renters currently cannot.
amountDisplay: Up to $2,250 for a heat pump and $1,000 for a heat pump water heater
incentives: Ductless multi-split heat pump (replacing electric heat): $750 per head, up to $2,250 | Ductless mini-split heat pump (replacing electric heat): $1,000 | Heat pump water heater (replacing an electric water heater): $1,000
eligibility: Suite in a purpose-built rental, strata condominium or equity co-op: low- or high-rise apartment, stacked townhome, or multiplex with six or more units; at least 12 months old | Year-round primary residence with a residential BC Hydro or City of New Westminster electricity account | Suite primarily heated by hard-wired electric heat | Heat pump must be a NEEP cold-climate model on the qualified product list, installed by an HPCN member | Strata council or co-op board approval; renters are not currently eligible | No income test; cannot be combined with the CleanBC Energy Savings Program condo rebate or other CleanBC, BC Hydro or FortisBC incentives for the same upgrade
howToApply: Get quotes and strata or co-op approval | Request a pre-approval code online from BC Hydro before buying or installing equipment (codes are valid for six months) | Complete the installation, pay the invoice in full and submit the rebate application within six months of the invoice date
notes: Rebates cannot exceed the invoiced and paid cost. Heat pumps invoiced and paid between August 1 and October 31, 2026 may earn an extra $500 (mini-split) or $1,000 (multi-split) bonus. If your household meets the income limits, the CleanBC Energy Savings Program condo rebate pays more.

name: takeCHARGE Insulation Rebates
administrator: takeCHARGE (Newfoundland Power and Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro)
summary: Electrically heated homes can get 75% of attic and basement insulation costs back, up to $1,000 per area plus up to $500 per area for professional labour, for a total of up to $3,000.
description:
The rebate covers 75% of the pre-tax cost of CSA-approved insulation (batt, rigid board, blown-in and spray foam) added to attics and to either basement/crawlspace walls or ceilings, not both. Spray foam must be professionally installed, and labour is only rebated when a participating professional installer does the job.

The home's primary heat must be electric (or the home must use at least 15,000 kWh a year if another source is also used), and it must have been built and connected before January 1, 2014. Approved rebates are credited to your electricity account.

takeCHARGE also offers a separate 50% rebate, up to $500, for insulating bare ductwork from an electric furnace or central ducted heat pump, and air sealing can be bundled with an attic insulation job.
incentives: Attic insulation materials: 75% up to $1,000 | Basement or crawlspace insulation materials: 75% up to $1,000 | Professional installation labour: Up to $500 per area | Duct insulation: 50% up to $500
eligibility: Homeowner or landlord with an active electricity account | Primary heat is electric, or annual use of at least 15,000 kWh | Home built and connected before January 1, 2014; primary residence on a permanent foundation | Must reach minimum R-values; topping up is rebated, full replacement is not
howToApply: Install the insulation and keep detailed receipts (number of bags, brand, R-value, coverage) | Apply online, or print the form and mail it to the utility that bills you for electricity | Approved rebates appear as a credit on your power bill, usually within 6 to 8 weeks
notes: Attics with no insulation, or where existing insulation is removed, are calculated from a starting value of R-20. Vapour barrier and studding are not rebated. If another program also rebates the insulation, the takeCHARGE amount is reduced so the total does not exceed 100% of the material cost.

name: Peak Smart Home Rebate
administrator: Yukon Energy Corporation with the Government of Yukon (Good Energy program)
summary: Yukoners on the main grid with electric heat or an electric water tank can get 75% back, up to $750 per device type and $1,500 per home, on eligible smart thermostats and hot water tank controllers when they join Yukon Energy's Peak Smart Home program.
description:
Peak Smart Home lets Yukon Energy make small, temporary adjustments to enrolled thermostats and hot water tank controllers when winter demand peaks, usually between October and April. Participants can override any event.

Enrolled households can get up to 75% of eligible purchase and installation costs back, to a maximum of $750 per device type: up to $750 for smart thermostats and up to $750 for a hot water tank controller, or $1,500 per home in total. Eligible devices include Mysa baseboard thermostats, a range of Sinopé thermostats, Sinopé hot water tank controllers and the Sinopé Zigbee gateway, with receipts dated after December 4, 2024.

You must sign up for Peak Smart Home before applying for the rebate. The Dependable Grid Program also offers a sign-up bonus and annual rewards for Peak Smart Home participants.
incentives: Eligible smart thermostats: 75% up to $750 | Eligible hot water tank controller: 75% up to $750
eligibility: Residential utility account holder on Yukon's main grid (Watson Lake, Burwash Landing and Old Crow are not eligible) | Devices control electric baseboards, an electric furnace or an electric hot water tank | A steady home internet connection (cellular internet does not qualify) | Enrolled in Peak Smart Home; receipts dated after December 4, 2024 | Tenants with their own Yukon Energy or ATCO Electric Yukon account can join (landlord permission recommended)
howToApply: Buy and install an eligible device (Yukon Energy does not install devices) | Sign up for Peak Smart Home at peaksmart.ca | Apply through the Good Energy Rebates portal with a paid receipt and proof of enrolment; the name on both must match | Allow up to 12 weeks for payment
notes: Check the eligible device list before you buy, and keep your receipt showing your name and a zero balance. Program support: 867-322-0183, 1-844-200-2153 or peaksmart@clearesult.com.

name: SaskEnergy Residential Equipment Replacement Rebate Program
summary: Rebates of $325 to $1,000 per unit when SaskEnergy customers replace natural gas heating or water heating equipment with a high-efficiency furnace, boiler, combi boiler, or tankless or condensing water heater.
description:
SaskEnergy pays a rebate when residential customers replace natural gas space or water heating equipment with a new high-efficiency model from its eligible equipment list. The current amounts are $325 for a furnace rated at least 97% AFUE, $750 per boiler plant (95% AFUE or better, up to 300 MBH), $800 for a combi boiler of at least 95% AFUE, and $1,000 for a tankless water heater (0.87 UEF or better) or a condensing water heater (0.80 UEF or better).

The equipment must be installed in a Saskatchewan home as part of its main space or water heating system by a gas contractor holding a valid Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan licence. Self-installs, used or rebuilt units, new construction and replacements of equipment still under the manufacturer's warranty do not qualify. Applications are due within 120 days of installation.

Heat recovery ventilators and standard storage-tank water heaters are not on the current eligible list. Revised program terms took effect August 17, 2026, and funding is limited.
incentives: Natural gas furnace, 97%+ AFUE: $325 | Boiler, 95%+ AFUE (up to 300 MBH): $750 | Combi boiler, 95%+ AFUE: $800 | Tankless water heater, 0.87+ UEF: $1,000 | Condensing water heater, 0.80+ UEF: $1,000
eligibility: SaskEnergy residential customer who paid the invoice and is the registered homeowner, landlord or rental company representative | New natural gas unit from SaskEnergy's eligible equipment list, used for the home's main space or water heating | Installed by a gas contractor with a valid TSASK licence; self-installs are not eligible | Not eligible: new construction, garages, gifted or prize units, or replacing equipment still under manufacturer's warranty | Separately metered row or duplex units and insurance-claim replacements can qualify
howToApply: Check that the model is on SaskEnergy's eligible equipment list before buying | Have a TSASK-licensed gas contractor install it | Apply online within 120 days of installation with the paid invoice | SaskEnergy pays by cheque, e-Transfer or bill credit within about six weeks of approval
notes: SaskEnergy can change or end this rebate at any time, so confirm your model on the eligible list before you buy. Saskatchewan has no provincial or utility heat pump rebate; the federal National Heat Pump Rebate is the main heat pump incentive to watch. Saskatoon homeowners can finance the rest of the cost through the Home Energy Loan Program.

name: takeCHARGE Air Sealing Rebate
administrator: takeCHARGE (Newfoundland Power and Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro)
summary: Rebates of up to $750 for air sealing in electrically heated homes, through three routes: new-home airtightness, blower-door-tested retrofits of existing homes, or air sealing bundled with an attic insulation job.
description:
takeCHARGE pays for measurable reductions in air leakage. For new construction, the rebate rises with how airtight the finished home is: $200 at 2.5 air changes per hour, $300 at 1.5, and $750 at 0.6 or better, verified by a blower door test within 12 months of the occupancy permit.

Existing homes earn $200, $475 or $750 for a 10%, 20% or 30%+ improvement between pre- and post-retrofit blower door tests. Homes built before 2014 that are getting an attic insulation upgrade can bundle air sealing done by an approved installer at $0.50 per square foot sealed, up to $750, paid to the installer. All homes need an HRV or air exchanger.
incentives: New construction airtightness (2.5 / 1.5 / 0.6 ACH50): $200 / $300 / $750 | Existing home, pre- and post-retrofit blower door tests (10% / 20% / 30%+ improvement): $200 / $475 / $750 | Air sealing bundled with attic insulation: $0.50 per sq. ft. sealed
eligibility: Primary heat is electric (existing homes may instead use at least 15,000 kWh a year) | Homeowner or landlord with an active electricity account | Home on a permanent foundation used as a primary residence, with an HRV or air exchanger
howToApply: Choose the pathway that fits your project | Have the required blower door test(s) done by an approved professional, or use an approved insulation installer for the bundled option | Apply online or by mail (the installer submits the bundled option); rebates are credited to your bill within about eight weeks
notes: The utilities may inspect the home within 15 months of processing. takeCHARGE may change or end the rebate at any time.

name: Kitchener Utilities Natural Gas Rebates
summary: Kitchener Utilities, the City of Kitchener's own gas utility, gives its residential customers a $75 bill credit for a smart thermostat and a $500 bill credit for upgrading to a condensing gas water heater.
description:
Kitchener Utilities is owned by the City of Kitchener and supplies natural gas to homes in the city. It runs its own rebates, separate from Enbridge Gas, for residential properties with an active Kitchener Utilities gas account.

The smart thermostat rebate is a $75 on-bill credit when you replace a manual or programmable thermostat with a smart model. It applies to detached, semi-detached and row townhouses heated mainly by a natural gas furnace or boiler, one per address. If the thermostat cost less than $75, you get the purchase price.

The condensing water heater rebate is a $500 on-bill credit when you replace a natural gas water heater with an ENERGY STAR condensing model rated 0.86 UEF or higher. Kitchener Utilities promotes it with its rental water heaters, and qualifying rentals include tankless and other high efficiency condensing models.
amountDisplay: $75 smart thermostat credit; $500 condensing water heater credit
incentives: Smart thermostat: $75 on-bill credit | Condensing natural gas water heater: $500 on-bill credit
eligibility: Residential property in the City of Kitchener with an active Kitchener Utilities natural gas meter and account. | Smart thermostat: detached, semi-detached or row townhouse heated mainly by a gas furnace or boiler, replacing a thermostat that is not already smart. | Water heater: replacing an existing natural gas water heater below 0.86 UEF with a condensing model at 0.86 UEF or higher. The current offers page says you must be the property owner and not already using a tankless water heater. | Credits go to the registered owner's utility account.
howToApply: Buy and install the qualifying equipment, and keep the paid invoice. | Apply online with the Smart Thermostat Rebate or Condensing Water Heater Rebate form on the City of Kitchener site, or call Kitchener Utilities at 519-741-2626. | Kitchener Utilities may inspect the installation before approving the credit.
notes: These rebates are only for Kitchener Utilities gas customers in the City of Kitchener. Kitchener Utilities says the programs can change or end at its discretion and funding is limited. If you are switching water heaters, it also offers a limited-time Switch and Save deal with six months of free rent on its rental water heaters.

name: BC Hydro Home EV Charger Rebate
summary: Rebate of half the cost of a Level 2 home EV charger, up to $350, with an extra $200 for a power management device.
description:
Owners of single-family homes, row homes and duplexes in BC Hydro territory can claim up to 50% of the purchase and installation cost of an eligible Level 2 charger, to a maximum of $350. Single-family home customers who install an EV power management device, which can avoid an electrical panel upgrade, can get $200 more.

Enrolling an eligible smart charger in BC Hydro's Peak Saver program earns a $250 bill credit plus $50 for each season you stay enrolled.

The charger must be new, bought (not leased) from a Canadian supplier, permanently mounted and installed with an electrical permit. The program is funded by the Province and run by BC Hydro and FortisBC. Combined incentives cannot exceed the total cost.
amountDisplay: Up to $350, plus $200 for power management
incentives: Level 2 charger (single-family, row home, duplex): Up to $350 | EV power management device: $200 | Peak Saver enrolment of a smart charger: $250 bill credit plus $50 per season
eligibility: BC Hydro customer in a single-family home, row home or duplex | Level 2 (208V or 240V) charger with a J1772 or NACS (J3400) plug on BC Hydro's rebate-eligible list; Tesla charging stations are no longer eligible | New, certified, purchased from a Canadian supplier, and permanently mounted at the home | Installed with an electrical permit; installing only a 240V outlet does not qualify | FortisBC electricity customers apply through FortisBC
howToApply: Pick a charger from BC Hydro's rebate-eligible list | Have it installed with an electrical permit | Apply online within 180 days of installation; approved payments are processed within 90 days
notes: Condo and apartment buildings use a separate multi-unit building charger program. FortisBC offers an equivalent home charger rebate of up to $350. The federal EV purchase rebate covers the vehicle, so it can be used alongside this charger rebate.

name: Énergir Smart Thermostat Grant (and Low-Income Supplement)
summary: Énergir natural-gas customers with central gas heating get $100 toward an ENERGY STAR smart thermostat. Low-income households can get an extra $220.
description:
Énergir, Québec's main natural gas distributor, offers $100 per eligible ENERGY STAR smart thermostat, capped at 75% of the device cost and limited to one per central gas heating system. It is open to current and future residential customers in single-family homes, duplexes, triplexes and residential buildings with central natural gas heating.

A low-income supplement adds $220 for a low-income owner of a single-family home or condo. For a home or building rented to low-income tenants, the supplement depends on the share of low-income units and is split 40% to the owner and 60% to the tenants. The supplement request must be filed before the thermostat is installed. Énergir also offers dual-energy and high-efficiency equipment grants, which are calculated individually in the Customer Space.
incentives: ENERGY STAR smart thermostat: $100 (max 75% of device cost) | Low-income supplement: +$220
eligibility: Current or future Énergir residential customer | Single-family home, duplex, triplex or residential building with a central natural gas heating system | Thermostat is ENERGY STAR certified and on Énergir's eligible list | Supplement: household income within Énergir's low-income thresholds (owner-occupant), or low-income tenants in the building
howToApply: Buy an eligible ENERGY STAR smart thermostat. If you want the low-income supplement, file the supplement request before installing it. | Install it yourself or through an Énergir partner. | Submit the grant request in your Énergir Customer Space within 30 days of the purchase date on your invoice.
notes: Énergir says amounts and terms can change without notice, and no end date is published. Check the current eligible-model list before you buy. Énergir's insulation and window grants are aimed at business and larger multi-unit customers, so they are not listed here. Dual-energy grants (a heat pump with gas backup) and high-efficiency equipment grants are shown individually in your Customer Space.

name: takeCHARGE HRV Rebate
administrator: takeCHARGE (Newfoundland Power and Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro)
summary: A $225 bill credit for installing an eligible high-efficiency heat recovery ventilator (or qualifying ERV) in a new or existing home with any heat source.
description:
Eligible HRVs, and some ERVs, must exceed set heat recovery and fan efficiency levels and be installed by an HRAI-certified installer. Homes with any heating fuel qualify, new or existing.

The rebate is credited to the electricity bill, usually within eight weeks of a complete application. The utilities may inspect the installation within 15 months.
incentives: Eligible HRV or ERV: $225
eligibility: Homeowner with an active electricity account | Home on a permanent foundation used as a residence | Model on takeCHARGE's eligible list, bought on or after September 15, 2013, and installed by an HRAI-certified installer
howToApply: Install an eligible model | Apply online or by mail with your receipt

name: In-Store Rebates
summary: Instant discounts at participating New Brunswick stores on smart thermostats for electric heat and on ENERGY STAR appliances, available until March 31, 2027.
description:
NB Power funds discounts taken off at the cash register at participating New Brunswick retailers, so there are no forms or mail-in claims.

Annual offers, available until March 31, 2027, cover smart thermostats for electric baseboard or in-floor heat and ENERGY STAR clothes washers, dryers, combination units, heat pump dryers, dehumidifiers and room air purifiers. Seasonal offers on smaller items such as weatherstripping, showerheads and programmable thermostats run until November 22, 2026.
incentives: Smart thermostat for electric baseboard or in-floor heat: $45 off | ENERGY STAR heat pump clothes dryer: $150 off | ENERGY STAR room air purifier: $75 off | ENERGY STAR washer/dryer combination: $60 off | ENERGY STAR clothes dryer: $40 off | ENERGY STAR clothes washer: $35 off | ENERGY STAR dehumidifier: $10 off | Seasonal items (weatherstripping, showerheads, programmable thermostats for baseboard heat, timers, motion sensors and more): $1 to $25 off per package
eligibility: Buy an eligible product at a participating New Brunswick retailer (limit of five items per transaction)
howToApply: Shop at a participating store; the discount is applied automatically at checkout
notes: Eligible products are marked in store, and availability varies by retailer; check with your local store.

name: Energy Conservation Assistance Program
administrator: BC Hydro and FortisBC, with Pacific Northern Gas (funded in part by CleanBC and the federal Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program)
summary: Free home energy evaluation and no-cost installation of upgrades such as heat pumps, insulation and draft-proofing for income-qualified B.C. households.
description:
ECAP sends a program contractor to evaluate an income-qualified home and then installs recommended upgrades at no cost. Depending on the home, this can include a heat pump or dual-fuel system (including switches from gas, oil, propane or wood), insulation, bathroom fans and draft-proofing.

On June 29, 2026 the province, the federal government, BC Hydro and FortisBC announced a $222 million expansion of ECAP, aimed at about 5,800 BC Hydro and 1,800 FortisBC households. Since August 25, 2026, Pacific Northern Gas customers can also apply. Apartments and condos are expected to become eligible in fall 2026.

You apply through the utility that supplies your main heating fuel. Meeting the income limit does not guarantee upgrades; what gets installed depends on the evaluation and available funding, and the program assigns the contractor.
amountDisplay: Free upgrades (no cost to eligible households)
incentives: Home energy evaluation and advice: Free | Heat pump or dual-fuel system: Free | Insulation, draft-proofing and bathroom fans: Free
eligibility: Combined pre-tax income of household members 18+ at or below: 1 person $51,100; 2 $63,600; 3 $78,200; 4 $94,900; 5 $107,600; 6 $121,400; 7+ $135,100 | Single-family home, townhome, row home, duplex, triplex, quadplex, or manufactured/mobile home (apartments and condos expected in fall 2026) | Any heating fuel: electricity, natural gas, oil, propane, wood or other fuels | A service address can take part only once every 10 years | Renters need a landlord consent form; strata units may need strata consent
howToApply: Check the income limits | Apply online or by paper to the utility that serves your main heating fuel (BC Hydro, FortisBC or Pacific Northern Gas); applications sent to the wrong utility are redirected | Submit proof of income dated within the last year for every adult in the home (tax summaries, T1, T4 and BC Assessment notices are not accepted) | Wait for approval (usually four to six weeks), then book the home evaluation with the assigned contractor | Approved upgrades are usually installed within two to three months
notes: First-come, first-served while funding lasts. ECAP is how the federal Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program is delivered in B.C., so the two are not separate offers. You cannot get ECAP and the CleanBC Energy Savings Program for the same upgrade. Households above the income limits can look at the Energy Savings Program or the Home Renovation Rebate Program. BC Hydro never asks for banking details or advance payment for this program. Outreach team: 1-888-798-7658.

name: Energy Savings Kits
administrator: NB Power (Save Energy NB) with funding from the Government of Canada and Province of New Brunswick
summary: Any New Brunswick renter can request a free kit of easy-to-install energy-saving products such as LED bulbs, a smart power bar, a water-efficient showerhead and draft-sealing supplies.
description:
The kits are aimed at renters who cannot make structural upgrades. Each typically contains LED bulbs and a nightlight, a smart power bar, kitchen and bathroom faucet aerators, a water-efficient showerhead, caulking cord, outlet and switch gaskets, and a drying rack.

Non-profit organizations can also order kits for their clients, and participants in some other NB Power programs receive them. Contents may vary.
incentives: Energy Savings Kit: Free
eligibility: You rent your home in New Brunswick, take part in an eligible Save Energy NB program, or are a non-profit ordering for clients
howToApply: Renters claim a kit through the online form on Save Energy NB | Non-profits email Kit@nbpower.com with who they want to help and how many kits they need
notes: Kit contents may vary.

name: Hilo Smart Home Service with Rate Flex D
summary: Customers on Hydro-Québec's Rate Flex D can get Hilo smart thermostats installed at no cost, or earn up to $210 for each compatible device they connect to Hilo, in exchange for letting Hilo cut heating during winter peak events.
description:
Hilo is Hydro-Québec's smart-home subsidiary. Customers who sign up for the dynamic Rate Flex D can get Hilo smart thermostats and the Hilo hub for $0, with installation included. Those who already own compatible thermostats or water heater controllers from Honeywell Home, Mysa or Sinopé can instead earn a bonus of up to $210 per connected device, up to 10 line-voltage thermostats, 2 low-voltage thermostats and 2 water heater controllers per address.

Under Rate Flex D, electricity is cheaper than the base rate for most of the winter (December 1 to March 31) but costs more during peak events: at most 30 per winter, 4 hours each, between 6 and 10 a.m. or 4 and 8 p.m. Hilo automatically lowers heating during those events. Hydro-Québec guarantees that new Flex D customers won't pay more than the base rate over their first full winter, and says customers can save up to 20% on winter bills.

The device credit and bonus are tied to a 12-month commitment. If you leave Hilo, or override automation during 10 or more peak events in the first 12 months, you must repay the remaining credit and a declining share of the bonus.
amountDisplay: Free smart thermostats + installation, or up to $210 per connected device
incentives: Hilo smart thermostats and hub: Free, including installation | Compatible connected device bonus: Up to $210 per device
eligibility: Hydro-Québec residential customer on Rate Flex D (or Rate D with the Winter Credit Option if enrolled before August 8, 2025), not on an off-grid system | Owners and tenants can join, as long as they hold the electricity contract | Single-family, semi-detached or row house, or a unit in a building of 2 or more units, with a Hydro-Québec communicating meter | High-speed internet with Wi-Fi covering the connected devices, and a smartphone for the Hilo app | Heating control requires electric heaters with a compatible connected thermostat
howToApply: Check your eligibility and order devices on the Hilo website (hiloenergie.com), or sign up for Rate Flex D in your Hydro-Québec Customer Space. | Book the installation, connect your devices in the Hilo app, and choose how strongly Hilo should reduce heating during peak events.
notes: Hydro-Québec's Winter Credit Option closed to new customers on March 31, 2026; only contracts already enrolled keep it. New customers who want to earn money from peak events should use Rate Flex D. You can leave Rate Flex D at any time by phone and go back to the base rate, but leaving Hilo early can mean repaying credits and bonuses. Read the current Hilo participant agreement before enrolling, since Hydro-Québec can change it with 60 days' notice.

name: Home Winterproofing Program
summary: Income-qualified households heated by Enbridge natural gas can get a free home energy assessment, plus free insulation, draft-proofing and a smart thermostat where needed.
description:
The Home Winterproofing Program installs energy upgrades at no charge in lower-income homes heated by natural gas. An authorized delivery agent spends about two hours assessing the home, and qualified contractors then install the wall, attic or basement insulation and draft-proofing the home needs. Participants who get insulation or draft-proofing also receive a smart thermostat. Expect at least three visits: the assessment, the installation and a follow-up.

One application screens you for both this program and Save on Energy's Energy Affordability Program, so eligible homes can also get electricity-saving items such as ENERGY STAR appliances and LED lighting. Renters can take part with the landlord's written permission. Enbridge says more than 65,000 homes have taken part.
amountDisplay: Free upgrades (no cost to eligible households)
incentives: Home energy assessment: Free | Attic, wall and basement insulation; draft-proofing: Free | Smart thermostat: Free | Energy Affordability Program add-ons: Free
eligibility: An Enbridge Gas account is in your name and the home is heated by a natural gas furnace or boiler, or by a gas fireplace that is the main heat source. | Before-tax household income is under the limit ($48,220 for 1 person, $68,193 for 2, $83,518 for 3, $96,439 for 4, $107,823 for 5, $118,113 for 6, $127,576 for 7 or more), or someone in the home receives Ontario Works, ODSP, LEAP, the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance for Seniors or Survivors, Healthy Smiles Ontario, OESP or Energy Affordability Program support. | Detached, semi-detached, duplex or triplex, row house or townhouse, or mobile home on a permanent foundation. Apartments and condominiums are excluded. | Renters need written landlord permission. Residents and providers of designated social housing can apply.
howToApply: Apply online through Enbridge Gas or call 1-844-770-3148. | Send proof of income (the latest Notice of Assessment for each adult in the home, with the SIN blacked out) or a benefit statement. | Host a home visit of about two hours from your area's delivery agent (EnviroCentre for K postal codes, CLEAResult for L, M and P, The Home Inspectors Group for N). | Contractors install the upgrades for free, and a follow-up visit confirms the work.
notes: Electrically heated homes should apply to the Energy Affordability Program instead. Some websites still show older, lower income limits; the limits here match Enbridge's current page. Homes built before 1980 have stricter insulation and draft-proofing requirements, but may still get help through the Energy Affordability Program.

name: LogisVert – Solar Panel Grant
summary: Hydro-Québec pays $1,000 per kW of grid-connected rooftop solar, up to 40% of the cost of buying and installing it.
description:
LogisVert pays a grant for new grid-connected solar panel systems installed on or after June 30, 2025. The grant is $1,000 per kilowatt of installed capacity, capped at 40% of the purchase and installation cost. For example, a 5 kW system costing $15,000 would receive $5,000.

The connection request must be filed by a master electrician, and Hydro-Québec must give final authorization to connect the system. Homes on a municipal or cooperative grid also need written authorization from that utility. Panels must be new, bought in Québec, and certified to CSA 22.2 No. 61730 and CSA 61215 or their UL or IEC equivalents. The whole system, including panels, inverter, wiring and racking, must be installed by a contractor with the right RBQ licences. Detached garages and sheds on the same lot are eligible locations.

Batteries, roof repairs, engineering plans and replacements of existing systems are not covered. On the Îles-de-la-Madeleine the grant is higher: $2,000 per kW, up to 50% of costs, but not for homes whose main heating is fuel-fired.
amountDisplay: $1,000 per kW, up to 40% of costs
incentives: Grid-connected solar PV (main grid): $1,000 per installed kW, max 40% of eligible cost | Solar PV – Îles-de-la-Madeleine: $2,000 per installed kW, max 50% of eligible cost
eligibility: House, multiplex, or residential building of 19 units or fewer in Québec (condos and larger buildings are not eligible for this measure) | System installed on or after June 30, 2025 | Final authorization to connect to the Hydro-Québec grid, or written authorization from your municipal or cooperative utility | New, certified panels bought in Québec | Complete installation by a contractor with the required RBQ licences; the connection request must be made by a master electrician
howToApply: Get quotes from licensed solar installers and confirm the system size in kW. Hydro-Québec recommends an installer experienced with grid-connected systems, ideally NABCEP-certified. | Have your master electrician file the connection request and obtain Hydro-Québec's final authorization. | Within 9 months of installation, submit a claim through the LogisVert portal (logisvert.ca) with your invoices, the connection authorization, the panel certificates and data sheets, and photos showing the panels.
notes: Systems installed from June 30, 2025 onward qualify, even if installed before the grant was announced. Home batteries are not covered by LogisVert. Since October 1, 2026, Rénoclimat pays up to $4,000 for a fixed home battery of at least 5 kWh in a principal residence. Grid-connected systems also fall under Hydro-Québec's self-generation (net metering) rules, so read those before you buy.

name: SaskEnergy Heating Affordability Program
summary: A free 96% efficient natural gas furnace, installed, for income-qualified homeowners whose furnace was made in 1999 or earlier; by invitation after SaskPower's Energy Assistance Program, for up to 50 homes until January 31, 2027.
description:
The Heating Affordability Program replaces old, low-efficiency furnaces in income-qualified homes at no cost. Each installation includes a new 96% AFUE natural gas furnace (95% for mobile homes), the venting changes it needs, three filters and a programmable thermostat if the contractor finds one is needed. SaskEnergy estimates savings of up to $650 a year.

There is no direct application. Homeowners first take part in SaskPower's Energy Assistance Program; if the home energy coach finds the home may qualify, SaskEnergy invites the household, CLEAResult verifies income and the furnace, and a SaskEnergy Network contractor quotes and installs the new furnace. SaskEnergy pays the contractor directly.

The current funding round runs from June 30, 2026 to January 31, 2027, or until 50 furnaces have been funded, whichever comes first. The program launched in 2025 and had replaced 37 furnaces before this round.

name: SaskPower Energy Assistance Program

description:
Through the Energy Assistance Program, a home energy coach visits income-qualified homes, shares ways to save and installs free products: LED bulbs, kitchen and bathroom faucet aerators, high-efficiency showerheads, pipe wrap, a block heater timer, a drying rack and, if the existing thermostat is compatible, a smart thermostat. SaskPower estimates savings of up to $230 a year.

The program is open to customers of SaskPower, Saskatoon Light & Power and Swift Current Light & Power who live year-round in a house, condo or apartment. Landlords who own detached, semi-detached or townhouse rentals with income-qualified tenants who pay their own utilities can also apply.

Taking part in this program is also the only way to be invited to SaskEnergy's free furnace replacement (the Heating Affordability Program).

name: Réno logement abordable – Affordable Housing Renovation Program (6+ Dwellings)
administrator: City of Montréal (Service de la stratégie immobilière et de l'habitation)
summary: Montréal pays 30% to 40% of renovation costs, up to $14,000 per unit and $500,000 per building, for older rental buildings of 6 or more units that keep at least a third of their rents affordable. Any oil-fired boiler, furnace or water heater must be replaced as part of the work.
description:
Réno logement abordable helps owners of older Montréal buildings with six or more dwellings renovate while keeping rents affordable. The city inspects the building and identifies the components that qualify. These can include heating, ventilation and air conditioning, the envelope and roof, foundations, windows and doors, and added thermal insulation.

The subsidy is a share of the cost of each component: 40% for the envelope, foundations, structure and roof, 35% for heating, air conditioning, ventilation and openings such as windows and doors, and 30% for electrical, plumbing and interior work. The caps are $14,000 per dwelling for work and $2,800 per dwelling for fees, with a maximum of $500,000 per building. Buildings with very affordable rents get 5 more percentage points, up to $16,100 per dwelling and $575,000 per building.

Replacing any oil-fired boiler, central furnace or water heater is mandatory, as is replacing the private part of a lead water-service line. You need an architect or other building professional, borough permits, and the city's written approval before any work starts.

name: Better Homes Ottawa Loan Program

summary: Ottawa homeowners can borrow $10,000 to $125,000 at a fixed 4.33% over 20 years for energy retrofits, repaid on the property tax bill. The program also offers per-ton heat pump incentives and a limited-time $600 loan reduction for EnerGuide assessments.
description:
Better Homes Ottawa offers 20-year, fixed-rate financing for energy retrofits, repaid as a local improvement charge on your property tax bill. It covers insulation, air sealing, ENERGY STAR windows and doors, green roofs, air-source and ground-source heat pumps, heat or energy recovery ventilators, thermostats, duct sealing, efficient water heaters, solar PV, battery storage, Level 2 EV chargers, and water-efficiency and flood-protection measures. Gas-fired equipment such as furnaces and gas water heaters is not eligible. A rental suite can be financed up to 30% of the loan.

You apply first and receive a Notice to Proceed; only costs after that date count. A pre-retrofit EnerGuide assessment is required, and you can request 50% of the estimated project cost up front, with interest charged only on the advance until the final payment. Projects should be finished within a year, and a 6-month extension is available.

For a limited time the program also pays heat pump incentives and a $600 loan reduction for completing EnerGuide assessments. You cannot get that reduction if you receive the $600 assessment rebate from Home Renovation Savings.

summary: Toronto homeowners can borrow up to $125,000 at a fixed low rate for energy upgrades and repay it on the property tax bill over up to 20 years. Heat pump-only and solar-only projects no longer need an EnerGuide assessment.
description:
The City of Toronto's Home Energy Loan Program provides fixed-rate financing for home energy improvements, repaid through your property tax bill. Eligible work includes air-source heat pumps, geothermal, windows and doors, insulation and air sealing, high-efficiency furnaces, boilers, air conditioners and water heaters, tankless and drain-water heat recovery systems, solar PV and solar hot water, battery storage, Level 2 EV chargers and toilet replacements.

Terms are 5, 10, 15 or 20 years. The 20-year term is only for projects that include heat pumps, geothermal, solar PV or new windows. Up to 30% of the funds can be advanced once the City approves your Property Owner Agreement. The loan stays with the property, so a buyer takes over the remaining balance, and you can repay early at any time.

Heat pump-only and rooftop solar-only projects do not need EnerGuide assessments before and after the work; the installer signs an attestation form instead. HELP can be combined with provincial, utility and federal rebates.

summary: Low-interest loans of $1,000 to $40,000 (up to $60,000 for deep retrofits) for Saskatoon homeowners, repaid on the property tax bill, plus a $1,000 rebate toward EnerGuide evaluations.

HELP lends Saskatoon homeowners between $1,000 and $40,000 for energy efficiency, renewable energy and water-saving upgrades, or up to $60,000 with proof that the project will cut home energy use by at least 50%. name: RénoPlex – Renovation Subsidies for Buildings with 1 to 5 Dwellings
administrator: City of Montréal (Service de la stratégie immobilière et de l'habitation)
summary: Montréal pays fixed amounts per item of renovation work, such as windows, doors, insulation, oil-heating replacement and envelope repairs, on modestly valued buildings of 1 to 5 units, plus a flood-protection stream.
description:
RénoPlex helps owners of Montréal buildings with 1 to 5 dwellings, including individuals, companies, co-ops and housing non-profits, renovate older, modestly valued buildings. The subsidy is a fixed amount per unit of work. Examples include $410 per replaced window, $550 per door, $700 per patio door, attic insulation at $3 per m² per R20 added, above-grade wall insulation at $4 per m² per R4 added, exterior foundation insulation at $9 per linear metre per R5 added, and $1,350 per dwelling for replacing an oil furnace with a central heat pump.

There are three blocks. Block 1 (1–5 units) covers foundations, plumbing, heating and air conditioning, electrical and similar work. Block 2 (2–5 units) adds the roof, building envelope, windows and doors, balconies and ventilation. Block 3 covers flood protection only, with a $500 minimum. Blocks 1 and 2 need a subsidy of at least $3,000. The subsidy is capped at 50% of actual costs and at $26,000 for a single-family home or $52,000 for 2–5 units. For co-ops and non-profits, amounts are multiplied by 1.5, up to $39,000 or $78,000 and 75% of costs.

You must not start work before the application is approved, which takes 3 to 4 months. After approval you have 18 months to finish, and borough permits are required.

summary: London homeowners can borrow up to $40,000 at a fixed 2.5% rate for energy retrofits and repay it on the property tax bill over 10, 15 or 20 years. Households under the income limits can also get up to $10,000 in incentives that reduce what they repay.
description:
BetterHomes London is the City of London's home energy retrofit financing program, launched in spring 2026 with support from the Federation of Canadian Municipalities' Green Municipal Fund. It lends between $5,000 and $40,000 at a 2.5% fixed rate. The project must be worth at least $15,000 and cut the home's energy use by at least 25%. You repay through your property tax bill over 10, 15 or 20 years, and you can pay it off early with no penalty.

At least 80% of the project cost has to go to energy efficiency work such as insulation, air sealing, windows and doors, heat pumps and other heating, cooling and ventilation, water heating, lighting, or solar and batteries. Up to 20% can go to related work such as electrical upgrades, EV charging, flood prevention, low-flow fixtures, permits and energy assessments. Up to half of the approved cost can be paid out before work starts, and the loan stays with the house if you sell.

Households under the program's income limits can earn incentives of $2,500 to $10,000, depending on how much energy the retrofit saves. The incentive is applied after the work is done and comes off your loan balance. A free retrofit coach helps plan the project, review quotes and find other rebates.

Rental properties can't get incentives. | Work already completed, appliances, cosmetic work and routine maintenance don't qualify.

description:
RetrofitWR is the Region of Waterloo's home energy retrofit program, running from 2026 to 2030 with funding from the Federation of Canadian Municipalities' Green Municipal Fund. The project must be worth at least $10,000 and cut energy use by at least 25%. Up to 40% of approved costs can be paid out before the work starts.

summary: Banff homeowners who cut their home's energy use deeply can earn a rebate of $125 for every gigajoule saved, rising to $250 per gigajoule beyond new-home performance, worth up to $20,000.
description:
The Town of Banff's Deep Retrofit Program pays for energy savings rather than for specific products. An EnerGuide evaluation before and after the work measures how many gigajoules (GJ) a year your home saves. The Town pays $125 per GJ of savings up to the rating of a typical new home of the same size and type, and $250 per GJ for any savings beyond that.

To qualify, the project has to close at least half the gap between your home's current rating and a typical new home, and at least half of the improvement must come from the building envelope, such as insulation, windows and doors. Homes generally need to be more than 20 years old and occupied year-round. Rental and staff housing can qualify.

The program launched with Banff's Clean Energy Improvement Program in March 2025. If you finance through CEIP you are considered for the rebate automatically and it reduces your loan balance. You can also apply for the rebate on its own.

description:
The City of Laval offers a subsidy to owners who replace their main oil-fired heating system, including a dual-energy system that uses oil, with one powered only by electricity or renewable energy, such as a heat pump, electric furnace or geothermal system. Converting to natural gas or propane does not qualify.

The amount depends on the type of building and whether the old system ran on oil only or was dual-energy: $2,000 or $1,000 for a single-family home, $1,700 or $850 for a mobile home, $1,400 or $700 for a semi-detached or row house or a condo, $1,400 or $700 per eligible unit in a duplex or triplex, and $900 or $450 per unit (up to 20 units) in a building of 30 units or fewer.

The old system, including the oil tank, must be fully dismantled and disposed of properly by a licensed electrician or plumbing and heating contractor. Replacements completed since September 5, 2017 can qualify. Under the current by-law, work must be completed by December 31, 2026 and the application received by January 31, 2027.

The City of Gatineau pays a subsidy to owners who remove an oil-fired central heating system and replace it with heating that runs only on electricity. The subsidy is 75% of the total cost of the work, up to $3,500 per eligible building, paid in a single payment once the work is done.

eligibility: Owner-occupant of a residential building in the eligible zone around the Saint-Hubert airport (see the city's eligibility map). | You must have received a Rénoclimat grant from the Government of Québec for the work. | The work must have been recommended in the Rénoclimat pre-work evaluation report and completed. | A City of Longueuil building permit must be obtained before any work that requires one.
howToApply: Check the city's eligibility map to confirm your address is in the zone. | Complete your Rénoclimat project and receive the provincial grant. | Send the PAI registration form to the Division des programmes (DAU.PAH@longueuil.quebec or 4300, chemin de la Savane, Saint-Hubert) with proof of ownership and residence, the building permit, the post-work Rénoclimat evaluation report, proof of the Rénoclimat payment and the blower-door test invoice if applicable.
notes: The city lists the PAI as active and says there is currently no waiting list. Funding is limited to the yearly budget, and requests are handled in order of receipt. The city asks for the post-work Rénoclimat evaluation report. Rénoclimat changed on October 1, 2026 and now has a simplified track where the evaluation is optional, so check with the city (311 or 450-463-7311) before choosing that track. The PAI can be combined with other City of Longueuil or Société d'habitation du Québec assistance.

name: Programme de retrait ou de remplacement des appareils à combustible solide non certifiés ou certifiés de première génération
summary: Québec City pays 90% of the cost of a new certified wood or pellet stove, insert, furnace or boiler, up to $1,000, when you replace an old uncertified or first-generation unit. Removing an old appliance without replacing it earns $100.
description:
The Programme de retrait ou de remplacement des appareils à combustible solide non certifiés ou certifiés de première génération (Program for removing or replacing uncertified or first-generation solid-fuel appliances) is a Ville de Québec grant under by-law R.V.Q. 2950. Its aim is cleaner air. It covers wood, pellet and other solid-fuel stoves, inserts, furnaces and boilers that are not certified to EPA or CSA B415.1, or that are first-generation certified models from about 1988 to 2015.

If you replace the old appliance with a new EPA or CSA B415.1 certified wood or pellet appliance, the city pays 90% of the cost, up to $1,000. The grant covers the appliance and the vent if one is needed, but not installation. A decorative gas fireplace qualifies only when it replaces an uncertified decorative fireplace. If you remove the old appliance and do not replace it, the city pays $100.

The city's authorized supplier picks up the old appliance at your home. Requests are processed in the order received while funds last, and no request can be reserved once funds run out. Any taxes or other amounts you owe the city are deducted from the grant.
incentives: Replace an old appliance with a new certified wood or pellet appliance: 90% of the appliance and vent cost, up to $1,000 | Remove an old appliance without replacing it: $100
eligibility: The appliance is in a residential building, an accessory building, or the residential part of a mixed-use building in Québec City. Commercial, industrial and institutional buildings are not eligible. | The old stove, insert, furnace or boiler is not certified to EPA or CSA B415.1, or is a first-generation certified model (about 1988 to 2015). | The owner applies. A tenant can apply with a signed proxy from the owner. | An owner can get more than one grant, for several appliances at one address or at different addresses.
howToApply: Before removing the old appliance, take a photo showing it still connected to the chimney, plus a photo of its label showing the maker and model. | Put the old appliance outside at ground level, not near the road, and email ville.poele@gmail.com with your name, address and phone number to book pickup by the city's supplier within five business days. | Within 6 months of pickup, email the completed form, photos and purchase invoice to Habitation@ville.quebec.qc.ca. | The city reviews your file and mails the payment.
notes: Not sure whether your appliance is certified? Send a photo of it and of its certificate or manual page through the city's 311 online form under "Autre demande". Don't put the old appliance near the street, because scrap collectors may take it before the city's supplier arrives. The supplier only handles pickup; for questions about the program call 418 641-6186 or email Habitation@ville.quebec.qc.ca. City rules also require you to declare any solid-fuel appliance you add, replace or remove within 90 days.

name: Bonification Rénoclimat, Chauffez vert et LogisVert – Energy Renovation Top-Ups
administrator: Ville de Repentigny (Service de l'urbanisme et du développement durable)
summary: Repentigny adds 25% to the grant you received from Rénoclimat (up to $500) or Hydro-Québec's LogisVert (up to $200). Owners who got a Chauffez vert cheque in the past 12 months can also claim 25% up to $500.
description:
The City of Repentigny tops up the provincial and Hydro-Québec grants that homeowners receive for energy-saving renovations. Once you have the cheque from the provincial or Hydro-Québec program, you send the city proof of it and receive an extra 25% by mail.

The top-up is 25% up to $500 for Rénoclimat (insulation, air sealing, windows and doors, ventilation, heating and other recommended work), 25% up to $200 for LogisVert (for example, a heat pump), and 25% up to $500 for Chauffez vert (replacement of oil or propane heating). Each request must be made within 12 months of receiving the provincial or Hydro-Québec cheque.
amountDisplay: 25% of your Rénoclimat or Chauffez vert grant (up to $500) or LogisVert grant (up to $200)
incentives: Rénoclimat top-up (insulation, air sealing, windows, mechanical systems): 25% of the Rénoclimat grant | LogisVert top-up (e.g. heat pump): 25% of the LogisVert grant | Chauffez vert top-up (oil or propane heating replaced with electric or renewable): 25% of the Chauffez vert grant
eligibility: Owner of a property in Repentigny. | You have received a grant cheque from Rénoclimat, Chauffez vert or Hydro-Québec's LogisVert for work on that property. | The request is made within 12 months of receiving the provincial or Hydro-Québec cheque.
howToApply: Complete your work and receive the grant from Rénoclimat, LogisVert or Chauffez vert. | Take a clear photo of the cheque and payment stub. | Submit the request online through the city's Mon compte portal (demandes en ligne). The top-up is mailed to you once the file is complete.
notes: The top-up is paid after the provincial or Hydro-Québec grant, so keep the cheque stub. Since October 1, 2026, Rénoclimat's energy evaluation is optional; files opened under the old rules still follow them. Contact the city's ecological transition team at 450-470-3830 or subventionenvironnement@repentigny.ca for help with the form. The heat pump top-up is a percentage of the LogisVert grant ("la Ville de Repentigny bonifie la subvention obtenue par le programme provincial LogisVert d'Hydro-Québec"), so it only adds to LogisVert, not to Énergir's dual-energy grant.

name: HAT Smart EnerGuide Home Evaluation Incentive
summary: Medicine Hat homeowners can get up to $250 back on a pre-renovation EnerGuide evaluation and up to $250 on a post-renovation evaluation, credited to their City utility account.
description:
HAT Smart, the City of Medicine Hat's conservation program, refunds part of the cost of an EnerGuide home evaluation on an existing home. The pre-renovation evaluation tells you which upgrades are worth doing, and the post-renovation evaluation confirms the savings. For 2026, each one can earn a rebate of up to $250, and the post-renovation rebate is new this year.

The evaluation must be done between January 1 and December 15, 2026, by an NRCan-registered energy advisor who holds a City of Medicine Hat business licence, and it must carry the HATSmart or CEIP program code. The same evaluation reports are needed if you later use the HAT Smart Existing Homes rebate or Clean Energy Improvement Program financing.

Rebates are handled first come, first served until the year's funding runs out, and they are credited to the utility account for the home.
amountDisplay: Up to $250 per evaluation (pre and post)
incentives: Pre-renovation EnerGuide home evaluation: Up to $250 | Post-renovation EnerGuide home evaluation: Up to $250
eligibility: The home is an existing home in Medicine Hat and you receive a City of Medicine Hat utility statement for it (electricity, natural gas and/or water). | The evaluation is completed between January 1 and December 15, 2026, under EnerGuide Rating System v.15. | The energy advisor is NRCan-registered and holds a current City of Medicine Hat business licence. | The evaluation carries the HATSmart or CEIP program identifier, and the advisor's paid receipt shows that code and their City business licence number. | Your City accounts must be in good standing. Condominiums are not eligible for HAT Smart residential rebates.
howToApply: Book an EnerGuide evaluation with a licensed advisor from the NRCan service organization list and ask for the HATSmart or CEIP identifier. | Pay the advisor directly and keep the paid receipt. | Submit the 2026 EnerGuide Evaluations rebate form online with your evaluation documents by December 15, 2026. | Allow about four weeks for the credit to appear on your utility account.
notes: The 2026 Existing Homes rebate is fully subscribed, but the EnerGuide evaluation rebate is still open. Combined government incentives cannot exceed the cost of the evaluation. Owners of rental homes can contact HAT Smart (403-529-8244, hatsmart@medicinehat.ca) about how the rebate is paid.

name: Programme d'aide financière à la transition écocitoyenne – EV Charger and Window Glass Grants
summary: Repentigny residents can get $150 for a home Level 2 EV charger installed by a licensed electrician. Owners can get up to $75 per certified sealed glass unit replaced in existing windows, up to $450.
description:
Repentigny's eco-citizen transition program refunds part of the cost of a range of green purchases. Two items help with home energy use.

A new Level 2 (240 V) charger that is eligible under the provincial program, bought from a Canadian store and installed at your home by a licensed electrician, qualifies for $150. Any resident can apply.

Owners who replace foggy, cracked or broken sealed glass units in existing window frames with IGMAC-certified (or equivalent) units get up to $75 per unit when bought in Repentigny (up to $450), or up to $60 per unit from another Canadian store (up to $360).

Requests must be made within 12 months of the purchase. Each property can make at most three requests a year across the program, and payment depends on the program still being in effect.
amountDisplay: $150 for an EV charger; up to $450 for window glass units
incentives: Home Level 2 EV charger (new, 240 V, installed by a licensed electrician): $150 | Replacement of defective sealed glass units (thermos) with IGMAC-certified units: Up to $75 per unit bought in Repentigny, or up to $60 per unit from another Canadian store
eligibility: EV charger: Repentigny resident with proof of residence. | Window glass: owner of a property in Repentigny. | Purchase from a Canadian store (higher amounts for Repentigny stores where offered), with a complete invoice. | Request made within 12 months of the purchase. Maximum three requests per property per year.
howToApply: Check whether your work needs a permit by calling the urban planning department at 450-470-3840. | Keep the invoices, installation invoice and before-and-after photos required for each item. | Submit the online request through the city's Mon compte portal, or in person at city hall. Payment is by cheque, usually 4 to 6 weeks after a complete request.
notes: City staff may visit within a year of the work to check it. Questions or help with the form: 450-470-3830 or subventionenvironnement@repentigny.ca.

name: Nanaimo Home Energy Assessment Rebate
summary: The City of Nanaimo pays $150 toward an initial EnerGuide home energy assessment and up to $200 more for a follow-up assessment that shows energy savings.
description:
Nanaimo homeowners can get part of the cost of an EnerGuide home energy assessment back from the City. The initial assessment rebate is $150. After you finish upgrades, a follow-up assessment earns $10 for every 5 GJ per year of improvement on the EnerGuide scale, up to $200, as long as the improvement is at least 5 GJ.

Funding is limited and paid first come, first served, with one application per property. The assessment must be done by an energy advisor whose service organization holds a City of Nanaimo business licence.
incentives: Initial EnerGuide home energy assessment: $150 | Follow-up EnerGuide assessment after upgrades: $10 per 5 GJ/year reduction, up to $200
eligibility: Project located in the City of Nanaimo; one application per property. | Assessment completed by an energy advisor with a valid City of Nanaimo business licence. | Apply within 24 months of the date on the assessment receipt.
howToApply: Book an EnerGuide assessment with a licensed service organization. | Apply online, by mail or in person at 411 Dunsmuir Street with the receipt and EnerGuide report. | For the follow-up rebate, submit the follow-up report showing the new rating and its receipt.
notes: The City says a typical assessment costs $400 to $500 for an existing home. Homeowners in the City's retrofit financing program can combine this $150 rebate with a separate $200 evaluation discount. The City can end the rebate without notice when funds run out.

name: HAT Smart Scratch & Win
summary: Medicine Hat utility customers can claim up to $100 per receipt, and up to $200 a year, on small energy- and water-saving purchases such as smart thermostats, weatherstripping and ENERGY STAR appliances.
description:
Scratch & Win is HAT Smart's rebate for small conservation purchases. You submit a 2026 receipt for an eligible item and City staff scratch a ticket on your behalf to set the rebate, which can be up to $100 per request. Each home can claim up to two requests, or one request worth up to $200, for a maximum of $200 in 2026.

The list is broad. It includes smart or programmable thermostats, weatherstripping, door sweeps, caulking and other air-sealing products, efficient lighting and smart plugs, home energy monitors, furnace and heat pump servicing, hot tub and pool covers, and ENERGY STAR dishwashers, fridges, freezers, washers, dryers, furnaces and air conditioners. Decorative lighting doesn't qualify.

The rebate is credited to your City utility account, usually within four weeks.
amountDisplay: Up to $100 per request, $200 per home in 2026
incentives: Energy- and water-saving products and ENERGY STAR appliances: Up to $100 per request (amount set by the scratch ticket)
eligibility: You have a City of Medicine Hat residential electric and/or natural gas utility statement in your name for the address. | Items were bought in Canada (in store or from a Canadian online seller) between January 1 and December 31, 2026. | Items save water, electricity or natural gas and appear on the HAT Smart eligible list. | Condominium associations are not eligible.
howToApply: Check that your item is on the eligible list on the Scratch & Win page. | Submit the 2026 Scratch and Win form online, or visit Customer Service at City Hall (580 1 St SE), with a dated receipt and proof of payment. | For ENERGY STAR items, include the brand, model number and the ENERGY STAR product finder sheet. | Staff scratch the ticket with a witness and credit the result to your utility account.
notes: Funding is limited and requests are processed in the order received, so the program can close before December 31 if money runs out. Incomplete requests are rejected and must be resubmitted. Questions: 403-529-8244 or hatsmart@medicinehat.ca.

name: Bornes de recharge électrique à usage domestique – Home EV Charger Grant
administrator: Ville de Boucherville (Direction des finances et des approvisionnements)
summary: Boucherville residents can get $150 toward buying and installing a home EV charger, on top of the provincial home charger grant. The charger must be installed by December 31, 2026.
description:
The Town of Boucherville pays a flat $150 to residents who buy and install a charging station at home for a plug-in electric or plug-in hybrid vehicle. It is a top-up to the Québec government's home charger grant, so you must first have that provincial application approved.

The charger must have been bought and installed at your home between December 8, 2020 and December 31, 2026, and the vehicle must have been acquired after December 8, 2020. The vehicle cannot be bought by or registered to a business, and the vehicle owner's spouse cannot apply in their place. Applications must reach the town by April 1, 2027. You also cannot owe money to the town.
incentives: Home Level 2 EV charger (purchase and installation): $150

Allow at least 60 days for processing.
notes: The town's page still refers to the home charging component of Roulez vert. The provincial home charger grant is now offered through Écorecharge, so ask the town (450-449-8115) which provincial approval it accepts if yours was issued under Écorecharge. The installation deadline is December 31, 2026, and the application deadline is April 1, 2027.

name: Nanaimo EV Charger Rebate
summary: Nanaimo adds a $150 top-up to BC Hydro's home EV charger rebate for houses, duplexes and townhouses, and helps apartment and condo buildings with up to $1,000 for an EV Ready Plan plus $100 per parking space.
description:
The City of Nanaimo tops up BC Hydro's EV charger rebates. Owners or residents of single-family homes, duplexes, row houses and townhouses can get $150 toward buying and installing an eligible Level 2 charger.

Apartment and condo buildings can get up to $1,000 for an EV Ready Plan and $100 per parking space for the electrical infrastructure the plan calls for. The City's criteria match BC Hydro's, but you apply to the City and to BC Hydro separately. Funding is first come, first served until it runs out.
amountDisplay: $150 for houses; up to $1,000 + $100/space for buildings

notes: Funding is limited, so check with sustainability@nanaimo.ca that money remains before you install. House applications must be in within 90 days of installation.

name: Subvention pour bornes de recharge résidentielles – Home EV Charger Rebate
summary: Terrebonne property owners can get up to $100 toward a home EV charger after the provincial grant, or up to $100 toward installing a charger they already have.
description:
The City of Terrebonne offers a small top-up to the Québec government's home charger grant. If you buy and install a charger, the city covers the cost left after the provincial grant, up to $100 before tax. If you only need installation of a charger you got for free or bought more than six months earlier, the city covers up to $100 of the installation cost.

Owner-occupants of houses and condo units, owners of rental buildings (for a charger all tenants can use), and condo syndicates (for a shared charger) can apply. Tenants cannot. Several requests are allowed per building.
incentives: Home EV charger purchase and installation: Remaining cost after the provincial grant, up to $100 (before tax) | Installation only (charger obtained free or bought more than 6 months earlier): Installation cost, up to $100 (before tax)
eligibility: Owner of a non-commercial residential property in Terrebonne: owner-occupant, non-occupant owner (for shared use by tenants in multi-unit buildings) or condo syndicate (shared use). | For purchase and installation, you must first have received the provincial home charger grant. | The charger must be installed within 6 months of purchase, and the request made within 12 months of purchase. | Tenants, private sales between individuals and home-made chargers are not eligible.
howToApply: Get the provincial home charger grant if you are buying a new charger. | Log in to your online file (Mes requêtes) on terrebonne.ca and create a request with two proofs of residence, proof of ownership and the purchase and installation invoices. | If you have no internet access, you can apply in person at the Bureau des citoyens, 708 A, boulevard des Seigneurs.
notes: Your file is only considered complete once all the documents have been received and checked by the program officer. The city's example assumes the $600 provincial home charger grant.

name: Red Deer Smart Thermostat Rebate
summary: Red Deer residents with a City utility account can get a $50 credit for buying and installing an ENERGY STAR certified smart thermostat in 2026.
description:
The City of Red Deer runs an annual rebate to encourage residents to switch to a smart thermostat. For 2026, the City credits $50 to your utility account when you buy and install a qualifying ENERGY STAR certified smart thermostat at a home in Red Deer.

The thermostat must be bought new in 2026 and appear on the City's approved product list. Only one rebate is allowed per utility account, and you can't get it if you've used the program before. Funding is limited: the City says "Applications will close when funds have been expended." The City's page no longer gives a closing date.
incentives: ENERGY STAR certified smart thermostat: $50
eligibility: You live in Red Deer and have a City of Red Deer utility account. | You bought a new smart thermostat from the qualifying list in 2026 and installed it at a property in Red Deer. | You haven't received this rebate before. | You aren't claiming the same thermostat under another funding program.
howToApply: Check the City's approved product list and confirm your wiring supports the thermostat (most need a C-wire). | Keep an itemized receipt showing the store, product, price and purchase date. | Submit the Smart Thermostat application form with your receipt.
notes: Apply early, because the City closes the program once the year's funding is used. Questions go to the City's Community Development team at 403-406-8820 or environmental.initiatives@reddeer.ca. The City's page does not state an end date (checked October 19, 2026); the thermostat must still be bought in 2026. Applicants must not be participating in other funding programs such as the federal Greener Homes Grant and Loan.

name: Banff Post-Purchase Rebate Program
summary: Banff residents can claim rebates after buying heat pumps ($750), heat pump water heaters ($500), windows (up to $200 each), efficient appliances and EnerGuide evaluations (up to $500).
description:
The Town of Banff's Post-Purchase Rebate Program pays residents back for a list of efficient products and services after they buy them. For homes, the energy items include $750 per heat pump, $500 per heat pump water heater, $650 for a solar water heater, $100 or $200 per window depending on efficiency, $100 per door, $300 for a fridge and $150 each for a dishwasher, clothes washer or ventless dryer.

An EnerGuide evaluation by an NRCan-registered advisor earns up to one-third of its cost, to a maximum of $500. The program also covers water-saving items and e-bikes.

Anyone who can show proof of Banff residency can apply, including renters. Receipts must be from the current or previous calendar year. The $500 furnace rebate ended in March 2025.
amountDisplay: $100–$750 per item; up to $500 for an energy audit
incentives: Heat pump (on NRCan list): $750 per unit | Heat pump water heater (on NRCan list): $500 per unit | Solar water heater: $650 per system | High-efficiency window replacement: $200 per window | Door replacement: $100 | Refrigerator: $300 | Dishwasher, clothes washer or ventless dryer: $150 each | EnerGuide energy audit: 1/3 of cost, up to $500
eligibility: You are a Banff resident with proof of residency, such as a current lease, a recent utility bill, a property tax bill or an employer housing agreement. | Receipts are from the current or previous calendar year. | Heat pumps and heat pump water heaters must be on NRCan's eligible product lists.
howToApply: Buy and install the eligible product or complete the energy audit. | Submit the Residential Post-Purchase Rebate application online with your receipt and proof of residency. | Questions: rebates@banff.ca or 403-762-1200.
notes: Furnaces no longer qualify for a post-purchase rebate, but they may still be covered by Clean Energy Improvement Program financing or the Deep Retrofit Program. Some Banff Access Program members get larger e-bike rebates. The Town says there is currently no limit on residential rebates per person or per household; energy audits are limited to one pre- and one post-audit per year.

name: BetterHomesTO Furnace Upgrade Program
administrator: City of Toronto, with Toronto Hydro
summary: Free virtual energy coaching from Toronto Hydro for Toronto residents thinking about replacing a furnace with a heat pump, with help finding rebates, financing and contractors.
description:
The City of Toronto and Toronto Hydro launched the Furnace Upgrade Program in September 2025 as part of BetterHomesTO. A Toronto Hydro energy coach gives free, personalized virtual advice on your home's heating and cooling options, explains which rebates and offers you may qualify for, and points you to contractors through Toronto Hydro's Cleantech Services Directory.

The program does not pay a rebate itself. For money toward the work, look at the Home Renovation Savings Program (heat pump rebates) and the City's Home Energy Loan Program (low-interest financing repaid on your property tax bill). The City has said the program will expand in 2026 to include heat pump installation services and targeted incentives for low- to moderate-income households; those details have not been posted yet.
incentives: Heat pump and furnace replacement energy coaching: Free
eligibility: Toronto resident, homeowner or tenant. | Low-rise home: detached, semi-detached, townhouse, row house or multiplex, including homes with basement or laneway suites.
howToApply: Book a free appointment through Toronto Hydro Energy Coaching. | Use the coach's advice to compare heat pump options and quotes, then apply to the rebate and loan programs that fit before you sign a contract.
notes: Coaching is free and does not commit you to anything. If your furnace has failed, book a coach before you sign a replacement contract: heat pump rebates through the Home Renovation Savings Program need pre-approval before installation.

name: Clean Energy Improvement Program (Alberta)
administrator: Alberta Municipalities, on behalf of participating municipalities
regions: Airdrie | Banff | Beaumont | Calgary | Canmore | Cold Lake | Devon | Drayton Valley | Edmonton | Grande Prairie | Jasper | Lac La Biche County | Leduc | Lethbridge | Medicine Hat | Okotoks | Pincher Creek | Rocky Mountain House | Spruce Grove | St. Albert | Stettler | Stirling | Strathcona County | Sturgeon County | Taber | Westlock | Wetaskiwin
categories: financing | heat-pumps | insulation | windows-doors | solar | water-heaters | heating-systems | air-sealing
summary: Property-tax-based financing that can cover up to the full cost of energy efficiency and renewable energy upgrades in participating Alberta municipalities.
description:
CEIP is Alberta's version of PACE (property assessed clean energy) financing. A participating municipality pays for qualifying upgrades, and you repay it through an extra charge on your property tax bill. Because the charge is tied to the property, it can transfer to the next owner if you sell, and you can pay it off early.

Financing can cover up to 100% of eligible project costs, with terms of up to 25 years depending on the upgrades and the municipality. Eligible work includes insulation, windows and doors, heat pumps, efficient heating and water heating, and solar panels. Each municipality sets its own interest rate, minimum and maximum amounts and intake windows.

27 municipalities list a residential CEIP. You must pre-qualify and have your project approved before work starts, and an EnerGuide home evaluation is part of the process.
amountDisplay: Up to 100% of project costs (limits set by each municipality)
incentives: Energy efficiency and renewable energy upgrades: Up to 100% of eligible costs
eligibility: Property owner in a municipality with an active residential CEIP | Property taxes and municipal accounts in good standing | Upgrades must be on the CEIP eligible list and installed by a CEIP-qualified contractor | Project must be approved before work begins
howToApply: Check whether your municipality participates at ceip.abmunis.ca and read its terms and conditions | Complete the short eligibility questionnaire, then submit the pre-qualification form | Get an EnerGuide home evaluation and work with a CEIP-qualified contractor on the project application | Sign the financing agreement once approved, then complete the work | Repay through your property tax bill
notes: Availability varies by municipality: Calgary's residential intake is closed until winter 2026/2027, and Edmonton is placing new pre-qualifications on a waitlist. Check your own municipality's page for its rate, limits and intake dates. CEIP is a loan you repay, not a rebate.

name: Energy Retrofit Assistance
administrator: Centre for Community Energy Transformation (CCET), a non-profit created by Brampton, Mississauga, Caledon and the Region of Peel
categories: low-income | energy-audits | heat-pumps | water-heaters | insulation | windows-doors
summary: Income-qualified households in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon can get a free EnerGuide home energy audit and selected upgrades such as heat pumps and insulation at no cost. It's a pilot with limited space, and applicants are added to a waitlist once it fills.
description:
Energy Retrofit Assistance is a pilot run by the Centre for Community Energy Transformation (CCET). CCET is a non-profit set up and funded by the City of Brampton, the City of Mississauga, the Town of Caledon and the Region of Peel. The pilot is for lower-income households in Peel whose homes are drafty, too cold in winter, too hot in summer or expensive to run.

If you qualify, you get a free EnerGuide audit from a certified energy advisor and help from an energy coach. Selected upgrades are then installed by vetted contractors at no cost to you. Depending on the audit, upgrades can include an air-source heat pump, a heat pump water heater, attic and wall insulation, and sometimes windows. The program says upgrades average about $11,500 per household. It also provides carbon monoxide monitors and helps you combine ERA with utility and other programs.

Applicants are prioritized by need, based on income, energy burden and the condition of the home. Space is limited. If the pilot is full when you apply, you go on a waitlist and may be referred to other programs.
incentives: EnerGuide home energy audit and energy coaching: Free | Selected upgrades (air-source heat pump, heat pump water heater, attic and wall insulation, some windows): Installed at no cost; about $11,500 per household on average
eligibility: You live in Mississauga, Brampton or Caledon and own the home or hold the gas or electricity account. Renters need the landlord's consent. | Household income is under the program limit (for example $47,090 for one person, $94,179 for four, $124,586 for seven or more). | You also qualify if you received benefits such as GIS, Ontario Works, ODSP, LEAP or OESP in the past 12 months. | Detached homes, townhomes and condos or apartments can apply. Applicants are prioritized by need.
