If your income is above the limit, CCET still offers a free 45-minute call with an independent energy coach for Brampton, Mississauga and Caledon residents. Enbridge Gas customers may also qualify for the separate Home Winterproofing Program, and electrically heated homes for the Energy Affordability Program.

name: HalifACT Home Energy Upgrade Program
summary: Owners of oil-heated Halifax homes built before 2000 can finance heat pumps, insulation and electric water heaters at a fixed 4.75% over 10 years, if the upgrades cut the home's energy use by at least half.
description:
The HalifACT Home Energy Upgrade program, launched in April 2026, finances deep energy upgrades for oil-heated homes in the Halifax Regional Municipality. The municipality pays your installers, then places a voluntary Local Improvement Charge on the property. You repay it once a year, separately from your property tax bill, over 10 years at a fixed 4.75%. You can pay off the balance at any time without penalty, and the charge can transfer to a buyer if both parties agree.

Eligible work includes heat pumps from Efficiency Nova Scotia's eligible list, removing the old oil tank and furnace, electrical service upgrades needed for the heat pump, duct changes, HRV/ERVs, electric water heaters and attic, basement, crawlspace and exterior wall insulation. The upgrades must be recommended in your home energy assessment and add up to an estimated 50% or greater cut in energy use. Solar isn't included, so use the Solar City program for that.

A free Navigator guides you through registration, the assessment, contractor quotes and the participant agreement. Financing is limited to about 100 homes.
incentives: Oil-to-heat-pump conversion and insulation financing (Local Improvement Charge): Covers approved upgrade costs at a fixed 4.75%, repaid over 10 years
eligibility: You own a residential property in the Halifax Regional Municipality that isn't used to earn business income. | The home was built before 2000 and is heated mainly with oil. | Property taxes and other municipal charges are paid up, and any municipal lien is paid or on a payment plan. | The recommended upgrades must achieve an estimated 50% or greater reduction in energy use, including the minimum heat pump and insulation specifications from your assessment. | The participant agreement must be signed by all owners and the municipality before installation starts.
howToApply: Register through the HHEU registration page or call a Navigator at 902-812-5028 (hfxnavigator@switchpace.org). | Book a home energy assessment (typically about $200) and send the report to the Navigator. | If a 50% reduction is achievable, get contractor quotes for the recommended upgrades and submit them. | Sign the participant agreement, have the work done, then complete the post-retrofit assessment. | The municipality pays the installers and adds the Local Improvement Charge to the property.
notes: Spaces are limited to about 100 homes, so register early. Ask your Navigator which Efficiency Nova Scotia or federal rebates you can apply for alongside the financing. Homes that don't qualify (for example, not oil-heated) can still use Halifax's Solar City financing for solar.

name: Home Energy Navigator (Greater Victoria)
administrator: Capital Regional District and local government partners (delivered by City Green Solutions)
summary: Greater Victoria homeowners can get free help from a local Energy Concierge to plan home energy upgrades, review contractor quotes and apply for rebates.
description:
The Home Energy Navigator is a free program created by the Capital Regional District (CRD) and local governments in the capital region. City Green Solutions, a local non-profit, runs it. After you register, an Energy Concierge holds a virtual home energy consultation, helps you choose upgrades, reviews quotes and helps with rebate applications. You also get a personalized retrofit guide.

The City of Victoria promotes the Navigator as its main support for homeowners. A limited-time offer of $75 enhanced EnerGuide evaluations for homes upgrading to heat pumps is now full and not taking registrations.
incentives: Energy Concierge support, virtual consultation and retrofit roadmap: Free | Neighbourhood Energy Navigator Offer ($75 enhanced EnerGuide evaluation): $75 evaluation (offer full)
eligibility: Homeowners in the capital region, including the City of Victoria. | Special offers are limited and open only in select communities when available.
howToApply: Register at homeenergynav.ca or call 1-866-381-9995 for help with registration. | An Energy Concierge contacts you to book a free virtual consultation.
notes: The Navigator does not pay rebates itself. It helps you find and apply for BC Hydro, FortisBC and provincial programs. City of Victoria residents with questions can also email sustainability@victoria.ca.

name: Home Energy Navigator (Kelowna)
administrator: City of Kelowna (delivered by City Green Solutions)
summary: Kelowna residents can book a free appointment with an Energy Concierge for help planning home energy upgrades and finding rebates. A limited number of fully subsidized EnerGuide evaluations are also available.
description:
The City of Kelowna partners with City Green Solutions to offer the Home Energy Navigator. After you register, an Energy Concierge holds a free virtual consultation, helps you work out which upgrades suit your home and priorities, and supports you through quotes and rebate applications.

For a limited time, eligible Kelowna residents can also register for one of a limited number of fully subsidized EnerGuide home evaluations through the program.
amountDisplay: Free advice; limited free EnerGuide evaluations
incentives: Energy Concierge support and virtual home energy consultation: Free | EnerGuide home evaluation: Fully subsidized (limited number)

name: Programme d'aides financières pour la transition écologique – Low-Carbon Heating and EV Charger Grants
administrator: Ville de Joliette (Service de l'Aménagement du territoire)
summary: Joliette tops up provincial and Hydro-Québec heating grants, including $500 per dwelling for a heat storage system for Hydro-Joliette customers. It also pays 25% of a home EV charger, up to $250 per connector.
description:
The City of Joliette's ecological transition grants include help for low-carbon heating and home EV charging. Most heating amounts are top-ups that require approval from a provincial or Hydro-Québec program first, and you must apply within 3 months of that approval.

Hydro-Joliette customers who install a heat storage system (accumulateur de chaleur) approved under LogisVert can get $500 per dwelling. The city also pays a grant when oil, propane or dual-energy heating was replaced with approval from Chauffez vert. For a detached house, that is up to $1,275 for oil, $850 for propane or $650 for dual-energy, or the cost of the work if lower. Lower per-unit amounts apply to semi-detached, row and multi-unit buildings, up to 20 units.

For home EV chargers, the city pays 25% of the after-tax cost, up to $250 per connector and $500 per site, in buildings of 1 to 4 dwellings. In buildings of 5 or more dwellings, it pays up to $500 per connector. A single-family home needs approval under the provincial home charger program first.
amountDisplay: Up to $1,275 per home for heating; $500 per dwelling for heat storage; up to $250 per EV charger connector
incentives: Electric thermal storage (heat storage) system, any replacement: $500 per dwelling | Oil heating replaced with low-carbon heating (Chauffez vert approval required): $1,275 (detached), $875 per unit (semi-detached, row, duplex, triplex), $550 per unit (4+ units, up to 20) | Propane heating replaced with low-carbon heating (Chauffez vert approval required): $850 (detached), $650 per unit (semi-detached to triplex), $225 per unit (4+ units, up to 20) | Dual-energy (electric/oil or propane) system replaced (Chauffez vert approval required): $650 (detached), $450 per unit (semi-detached to triplex), $275 per unit (4+ units, up to 20) | Home EV charger, building of 1 to 4 dwellings: 25% of after-tax cost, up to $250 per connector | EV charger, building of 5 or more dwellings: 25% of after-tax cost, up to $500 per connector
eligibility: Owner of a residential building in Joliette. | Heat storage: Hydro-Joliette customer with an approved LogisVert application. | Oil, propane or dual-energy replacement: approved Chauffez vert application. | EV charger: proof of ownership or residence and invoices for the charger and installation. Single-family homes and buildings of 5+ units need provincial home charger approval. | The request must be made within 3 months of the provincial or Hydro-Québec approval.
howToApply: Get your LogisVert, Chauffez vert or provincial home charger approval first. | Download the city's form for heating equipment or for EV chargers from the Programmes et subventions page. | Send the form with proof of ownership, purchase and installation invoices and proof of approval to the Service de l'Aménagement du territoire, 614, boulevard Manseau, or urbanisme@ville.joliette.qc.ca. | The city may inspect the installation before paying.
notes: The amounts come from the city's 2024 table of grants. Confirm current amounts with the Service de l'Aménagement du territoire (450-753-8000). Québec's Chauffez vert program closed on March 31, 2026, so the oil, propane and dual-energy top-ups only help owners whose Chauffez vert approval is recent enough to apply within the city's 3-month window. The city also has separate grants for replacing or removing wood stoves.

name: Rental Apartment Retrofit Accelerator Pilot (City of Victoria)
administrator: City of Victoria (applications guided by LandlordBC)
summary: Owners of older gas-heated rental apartment buildings in Victoria can get a municipal property tax exemption covering up to 100% of eligible costs to switch to electric heating or hot water, for up to 10 years.
description:
The City of Victoria's Rental Apartment Retrofit Accelerator pilot, launched in May 2024, offers a revitalization tax exemption to owners of market rental buildings that switch from gas to electric space heating, hot water or both. The exemption can cover up to 100% of eligible costs, spread over a term of up to 10 years. Only municipal property taxes are exempted, not school or other levies.

The bylaw limits the pilot to five buildings in total, with up to three in the emissions reduction stream. LandlordBC guides owners through planning and the application.
amountDisplay: Municipal property tax exemption up to 100% of eligible costs, up to 10 years
incentives: Gas to electric space heating and/or hot water (GHG Emissions Reduction Stream): Municipal tax exemption up to 100% of eligible costs
eligibility: Market rental building within City of Victoria boundaries, three to six storeys, with at least 10 dwelling units. | Uses natural gas for hot water, space heating or both, and was built before January 1, 2000. | No active building or development permit for the work, and no outstanding taxes or charges owing to the City. | Work must be completed within two years of the City accepting the application.
howToApply: Contact LandlordBC through LandlordBC.ca/RARA to plan the project and prepare the application. | Apply to the City in writing with the required documents, such as a BC Hydro program application or an engineer's energy study, and an electrical capacity assessment. | Questions can go to sustainability@victoria.ca.
notes: Spaces are very limited, so ask the City whether one is still open before you commit to design work. The City's page has a tax savings estimator. A tenant assistance plan is needed if tenants may be displaced.

name: Retrofit Assist
administrator: Community Energy Association, with participating local governments
summary: Residents of Kamloops, Squamish, Whistler and the East Kootenay get free concierge help with home energy retrofits and, for a limited time, an EnerGuide evaluation for $99 plus tax, which the program says saves $500 or more.
description:
Retrofit Assist is a free home retrofit concierge run by the non-profit Community Energy Association in partnership with local governments. An advisor talks through your goals, explains rebates and financing, helps you plan upgrades such as air sealing, insulation, windows, heat pumps and solar, and connects you with Energy Advisors and contractors.

While subsidies last, participants can book a pre-retrofit EnerGuide evaluation for $99 plus tax, which the program says saves $500 or more. The team also helps arrange the post-retrofit evaluation and make the most of available rebates and loans.
incentives: Retrofit concierge support (planning, rebates, contractor connections): Free | Subsidized pre-retrofit EnerGuide evaluation: $99 plus tax (saves $500 or more)
eligibility: Residents of a participating community: Kamloops, Squamish, Whistler or the East Kootenay. | Homeowners and renters can take part.
howToApply: Apply online at retrofitassist.ca/apply or at a community event. | A Retrofit Assist advisor follows up to discuss your needs and set up an EnerGuide evaluation.
notes: Retrofit Assist stopped taking new participants in Rossland at the end of 2025. Ask your advisor which provincial, utility and federal rebates currently apply to your project. Contact: info@retrofitassist.ca or 236-576-2502.

name: Solar City
summary: Halifax property owners can finance a solar installation through the municipality at a fixed rate and repay it over ten years as a charge separate from their tax bill.
description:
Solar City lends property owners the cost of a solar system; the municipality pays the contractor once the installation is certified, and the owner repays through a local improvement charge over ten years at a fixed 4.75% rate. There is no credit check, but municipal accounts must be in good standing.

Owners can pay off the balance early without penalty. If the home is sold first, the balance can be paid at closing or passed on to the buyer. Any rebates are claimed by the owner separately and are not deducted from the amount owed.

Residential owners, non-profits, co-ops, charities and places of worship within HRM are eligible. Only roof areas producing at least 70% of an optimal system's output can be financed.
incentives: Solar system financing: Fixed 4.75% over 10 years
eligibility: Property within Halifax Regional Municipality boundaries | Property taxes and other municipal charges in good standing | All legal owners sign the participant agreement
howToApply: Register online with the Solar City program office and receive a project ID | Get quotes from at least three solar contractors and tell the office which one you selected | Sign the participant agreement once staff review the contractor's documents | After installation is certified, the municipality pays the contractor and you receive a repayment schedule
notes: Solar City is financing, not a rebate; the provincial SolarHomes rebate is closed. Confirm the current interest rate and terms with the Solar City office (solarcity@halifax.ca) before you sign the participant agreement.

name: Strata Energy Advisor (Victoria and Saanich)
administrator: Zero Emissions Innovation Centre, in partnership with the City of Victoria and District of Saanich
summary: Condo stratas in Victoria and Saanich that use natural gas can get a free energy advisor and a decarbonization plan for the building.
description:
The City of Victoria launched the Strata Energy Advisor program in 2024 with the District of Saanich and the Zero Emissions Innovation Centre (ZEIC). An energy advisor works with the strata council, reviews whole-building utility data, visits the building and a few suites, and prepares a free plan that times upgrades like heat pumps with replacements the building already needs.

The service is free to the strata. It is meant for apartment-style condo buildings that still use natural gas for heating, hot water, ventilation or fireplaces.
amountDisplay: Free energy advisor and decarbonization plan

howToApply: Take the eligibility quiz and register on the ZEIC Strata Energy Advisor page (strataenergyadvisorbc.ca). | An advisor contacts the strata to review eligibility and goals, then the strata signs a participant agreement.

name: Seniors Aging in Place Program
summary: Senior NWT homeowners within their community's income threshold can get a forgivable loan of up to $15,000 a year for upgrades that lower heating, power and water costs, or for minor accessibility changes; the 2026 intake closes October 31.
description:
Housing NWT helps seniors stay in their homes with a forgivable loan of up to $15,000 over one year. It covers upgrades that make a home more efficient and cheaper to heat, power and supply with water, as well as minor adaptations such as grab bars. More than one unrelated repair can be approved in a year as long as the total stays within $15,000.

One homeowner must be 60 or older, and household income must be within the monthly income threshold for your community. Households earning more than $59,999 pay 10% of the repair cost before work begins.

Applications for 2026 are accepted from April 1 to October 31, 2026, and successful applicants are told within 60 days after the intake closes. You can apply to this program and to the Seniors Home Repair program, which offers a forgivable loan of up to $50,000 for larger health and safety repairs.
incentives: Efficiency upgrades and minor accessibility adaptations: Forgivable loan up to $15,000 per year
eligibility: At least one homeowner aged 60 or older | Lived in the NWT for three years and in the home for more than a year | Household income within the monthly Core Need Income Threshold for your community | Home within municipal boundaries with continuous power, potable water, heat and a working sewage system | Mortgage, land, lease or tax arrears may affect eligibility
howToApply: Phone your Housing NWT district office before October 31, 2026 | Complete the application with a Housing NWT representative (it cannot be completed on your own) | Take part in the required client counselling; district technical staff plan the work with you
notes: Applications are completed with Housing NWT staff and counselling is required, so call your district office well before October 31. Seniors who need larger health and safety repairs can also apply to the Seniors Home Repair program.

name: BC Hydro Air Source Heat Pump Bonus Rebate (Fall 2026)
summary: A limited-time extra $500 to $1,000 for BC Hydro customers who replace electric heat with an eligible air source heat pump installed, invoiced and paid between August 1 and October 31, 2026.
description:
BC Hydro is paying a temporary bonus on top of its regular electric-to-heat-pump rebates. Under the Home Renovation Rebate Program, a whole-home heat pump earns an extra $1,000 and a partial-home heat pump an extra $500. Under the Condo and Apartment Rebate Program, a ductless multi-split earns an extra $1,000 and a single mini-split an extra $500.

The installation must be completed, invoiced and paid in full between August 1 and October 31, 2026, and the complete rebate application must be in by November 30, 2026. Condo and apartment applicants need BC Hydro pre-approval before installing. The bonus is paid as a credit on your BC Hydro bill.

Funding is limited and handed out first-come, first-served. Total rebates cannot exceed the invoiced and paid cost. BC Hydro customers aged 19 or older can also enter a contest for one of three $5,000 prizes.
incentives: Whole-home heat pump (Home Renovation Rebate Program): $1,000 | Partial-home heat pump (Home Renovation Rebate Program): $500 | Ductless multi-split heat pump (Condo and Apartment Rebate Program): $1,000 | Ductless mini-split heat pump (Condo and Apartment Rebate Program): $500
eligibility: BC Hydro customer in good standing, with any outstanding balance paid | Air source heat pump that replaces an existing electric heating system and meets the Home Renovation Rebate or Condo and Apartment Rebate requirements | Installation completed, invoiced and fully paid between August 1 and October 31, 2026 | Complete rebate application submitted by November 30, 2026
howToApply: Have an HPCN contractor finish the installation and pay the invoice in full by October 31, 2026 | Condo and apartment owners: get BC Hydro pre-approval before the work starts | Submit the regular heat pump rebate application by November 30, 2026; the bonus is assessed with it

Only electric-to-heat-pump upgrades qualify; other upgrades in the same project do not earn the bonus. After October 31, only the regular rebates apply.

name: myEnergy Rewards
summary: Hydro One customers in eligible postal codes can get a $100 prepaid card for enrolling a compatible smart thermostat in its demand-response program. The current offer ends November 30, 2026, or earlier if spots run out.
description:
myEnergy Rewards is Hydro One's own smart-thermostat demand response program, offered as an alternative to the province's Peak Perks. On high-demand days you get a notice, and your enrolled thermostat is adjusted slightly to ease load on the grid, sometimes after a short pre-cool. You can override any adjustment.

The current offer gives new applicants a $100 prepaid credit card once their thermostat is connected and enrolment is confirmed. It is limited to the first 5,500 eligible applicants and ends November 30, 2026. Hydro One also runs an invitation-only EV managed-charging pilot that pays up to $100.
incentives: Smart thermostat enrolment: $100 | EV managed charging pilot: Up to $100
eligibility: Hydro One residential or small business customer in an eligible postal code (check with Hydro One's eligibility tool). | Compatible HVAC smart thermostat (Sensi, ecobee, Google Nest or Honeywell models) and stable, always-on Wi-Fi. | You cannot be enrolled in Save on Energy's Peak Perks at the same time.
howToApply: Check your postal code on Hydro One's myEnergy Rewards page. | Click Enrol now, choose your thermostat brand, and follow the prompts on the partner platform. | Connect the thermostat. The reward is sent once enrolment is confirmed.
notes: The $100 offer is limited to the first 5,500 new applicants and ends November 30, 2026, or earlier if spots run out. The postal-code limit applies only to new applicants; current members stay enrolled. Hydro One customers outside eligible areas can join Peak Perks instead. Questions: 1-866-658-1878 or myenergyrewards@hydroone.com.

name: Nanaimo Home Energy Retrofit Financing Program
categories: financing | heat-pumps | insulation | windows-doors | air-sealing | solar | batteries
summary: Nanaimo homeowners can borrow up to $15,000 interest-free for heat pumps, insulation, windows and doors, solar and batteries, repaid over 10 years on the property tax bill. The current intake runs September 14 to October 31, 2026.
description:
The City of Nanaimo's Home Energy Retrofit Financing Program is a property-tax (PACE-style) loan of up to $15,000 at 0% interest. You repay it over 10 years through a charge on your property tax bill; for example, $15,000 works out to $1,500 a year. You can pay off the whole balance early, and up to 25% of the project cost (maximum $5,000) can be advanced for a contractor deposit.

Eligible work includes switching from fossil fuel heating to an all-electric heat pump (dual-fuel systems are excluded), solar panels on homes that already heat with electricity, batteries where solar is already installed, and envelope upgrades such as insulation, windows, doors and draft-proofing. Up to 30% of the loan can go to related non-energy work done alongside an energy upgrade.

The program targets middle-income households: incomes must be above the CleanBC Energy Savings Program Level 1 threshold (unless you are already in that program) and below the City's 90th-percentile limits. Applications are ranked on income and equity, energy savings and climate impact, with priority for seniors. Participants must join the free Home Energy Navigator and get EnerGuide evaluations before and after the work.
incentives: Home energy retrofit loan (heat pump, envelope, solar, battery): Up to $15,000 at 0%, repaid over 10 years on property taxes | Pre-upgrade EnerGuide evaluation discount for financing participants: $200 off
eligibility: Property within City of Nanaimo boundaries with an assessed value of $1.23 million or less, and property taxes up to date. | Household income must be below the City's 90th-percentile limits ($185,505 for one person up to $344,712 for four or more) and above the CleanBC Energy Savings Program Level 1 threshold, unless you are already accepted in that program. | Only the property owner can apply and sign. Second homes you own are eligible. | You must complete a pre-upgrade EnerGuide evaluation, use an approved contractor, join the free Home Energy Navigator, and sign the financing agreement before work begins.
howToApply: Check with your mortgage lender that the program does not conflict with your mortgage terms. | Submit the online application by October 31, 2026, or apply in person at the Service and Resource Centre, 411 Dunsmuir Street, with your latest Notice of Assessment for every adult in the home and proof of ownership. | If accepted, sign the petition to Council, get a pre-upgrade EnerGuide evaluation and contractor quotes, then sign the financing agreement before work starts.
notes: If you qualify for the CleanBC Energy Savings Program, apply there first; City financing can then cover eligible costs the rebate does not. The cost of the post-upgrade EnerGuide evaluation can be included in the loan. An EnerGuide evaluation done on or after April 1, 2024 may be reusable if no work has started. Questions: retrofit.financing@nanaimo.ca.

name: Affordable Heat Pump Program
administrator: Government of Yukon, Energy Branch (Energy, Mines and Resources) with federal funding
summary: Lower- and median-income Yukon homeowners can have up to 100% of a heat pump's purchase and installation covered, to a maximum of $24,000; demand has exceeded funding and new applicants have been waitlisted.
description:
The Affordable Heat Pump Program launched in December 2024 and was fully subscribed within weeks; later applicants were placed on a waitlist in the order they applied. Federal and territorial funding was increased in March 2025.

The share of costs covered depends on household income, up to 100% and $24,000. Homes switching from oil heat also received a $250 upfront payment through the federal partner program. Approval is required before installation.

Homeowners who do not qualify can use the standard Good Energy heat pump rebate (50% up to $10,500) instead.
incentives: Heat pump purchase and installation: Up to 100% of cost, max $24,000 | Homes switching from oil heat: $250 upfront
eligibility: After-tax household income below: 1 resident $53,820; 2 $110,400; 3 $139,150; 4 $163,300; 5+ $184,000 | Own the home in Yukon | Pre-approval required before installation
howToApply: Contact the Energy Branch (energy@yukon.ca, 867-393-7063) to apply or join the waitlist before installing | Do not install until you have written approval

name: Enhanced Energy Savings Program
summary: New Brunswick homeowners with household income of $70,000 or less can get insulation, ventilation and, where suitable, a heat pump at no cost, but new registrations are on a waiting list that NB Power says could be up to two years.
description:
EESP targets homes that need major efficiency work, especially insulation and air sealing. After registration and income verification, a service organization performs a pre-upgrade evaluation and an NB Power-approved contractor of your choice carries out the approved work, followed by a post-upgrade evaluation.

Mini-split heat pumps installed through the program come with a 10-year parts and labour warranty and three free deep cleanings. Homes leaving oil heat have the oil tank, furnace or boiler removed and disposed of at no cost.

The program is open regardless of heating fuel or electricity provider, including customers of Saint John Energy, Edmundston Energy and Perth-Andover. NB Power says the program is fully subscribed for 2025/26 and beyond for new registrations and is keeping a waiting list.
incentives: Basement, attic and wall insulation; air sealing: No cost | Ventilation for air quality or moisture: No cost | Mini-split heat pump: No cost where eligible | Oil heating replacement and oil system removal: No cost where approved
eligibility: You own the home in New Brunswick and live in it | Combined gross household income of $70,000 or less (line 15000 of each adult's Notice of Assessment, adults 19 and over) | Any heating type and any electricity provider
howToApply: Register online and upload each adult's latest CRA Notice of Assessment (couples who split pension income send both full T1 returns instead) | New registrations go on a waiting list; do not reapply or call to check your place | When funding allows, NB Power sends an acceptance letter or email and a service organization books the pre-upgrade evaluation | An approved contractor completes the work, followed by a post-upgrade evaluation
notes: Heat pumps are not guaranteed; they depend on the evaluation, and the program does not reimburse heat pumps you buy yourself or repair rental units. If you want to keep your oil tank, or you would rather not wait, the Total Home Energy Savings Program offers rebates instead. NB Power says you can benefit from both programs, but "Programs must be completed one at a time," and a measure paid under Total Home can't also be paid by another NB Power program.

name: City of Edmonton Residential Clean Energy Improvement Program

summary: Edmonton's property-tax financing for home energy upgrades, from $3,000 up to $50,000 at a fixed 6% rate; new pre-qualifications are being waitlisted.
description:
Edmonton's CEIP finances up to 100% of eligible residential energy upgrades, with a minimum of $3,000 and a maximum of $50,000. Repayment is added to the property tax bill at a fixed 6% rate over up to 20 years (or the useful life of the upgrades, if shorter), and can be paid off early without penalty.

Residential projects need at least three upgrades, unless fewer are needed to reach net zero or the property has used CEIP before. Heat pumps, solar, windows, doors, insulation, water heating and lighting qualify. Air conditioners, gas furnaces not paired with a heat pump, and standard storage water heaters do not.

The City says the program is nearing capacity, so new pre-qualification submissions go on a waitlist and are processed first-come, first-served as space is confirmed.
incentives: Eligible efficiency and renewable upgrades (minimum three): $3,000 to $50,000

howToApply: Complete the CEIP pre-qualification form through Alberta Municipalities; it will be placed on the waitlist | When invited, get an EnerGuide home evaluation and choose CEIP-qualified contractors | Submit the project application, sign the agreements, complete the work and a post-project EnerGuide evaluation | Repay through your property tax bill
notes: Being waitlisted does not guarantee financing. Edmonton's earlier rebate programs, the Home Energy Retrofit Accelerator and the solar rebate, are closed.

name: Guelph Greener Homes
categories: financing | heat-pumps | insulation | windows-doors | air-sealing | water-heaters | solar | low-income
summary: Guelph offers 0% interest loans of up to $50,000 for home energy upgrades, but loan funding is nearly used up and new applicants go on a waitlist. Low-income households can still apply for grants of up to $15,000 toward an air-source heat pump.
description:
Guelph Greener Homes provides interest-free loans of up to $50,000 with no admin fee, repaid over 10 years through the property tax bill. A 20% down payment, to a maximum of $10,000, is required. Eligible upgrades include insulation, air sealing, windows and doors, air-source and cold-climate heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, heat recovery, solar PV and solar hot water. Thermostats only qualify alongside other upgrades.

Loan funding is almost fully committed, so new applicants join a waitlist. A separate grant of up to $15,000 for air-source heat pumps is still available to low-income homeowners whose property is assessed at $350,000 or less. Grant recipients must pay 50% of the project cost.
amountDisplay: 0% loans up to $50,000; low-income heat pump grants up to $15,000
incentives: Zero-interest retrofit loan: Up to $50,000 | Low-income air-source heat pump grant: Up to $15,000
eligibility: Low-rise residential property in Guelph with a City tax account, more than 5 years old. All registered owners consent. | No back taxes, liens or title disputes, and work has not started. | Enrol in a 12-month pre-authorized payment plan for property taxes and loan repayment. | Grant only: primary residence, current value assessment of $350,000 or less, and household income under the limits.
howToApply: Register through the program's online portal (loan applicants join the waitlist). | Once approved, submit a pre-retrofit energy audit and contractor quotes to request funds. | Complete the work, then submit a post-retrofit audit and invoices to receive the final payment.
notes: Loan funding is almost fully committed, so new loan applicants join a waitlist and are served first come, first served while funds last. Grants for air-source heat pumps are still available to low-income homeowners while funding lasts. Pre- and post-retrofit energy audits are required. Contact the program at 519-822-1260 ext. 3984.

name: Calgary Home Upgrades Program
administrator: City of Calgary, delivered by Kambo Energy Group
categories: insulation | air-sealing | heating-systems | water-heaters | energy-audits | low-income
summary: Free home energy upgrades, such as insulation and efficient furnaces, for income-qualified Calgary homeowners and renters; the upgrades stream is taking waitlist applications.
description:
The City of Calgary funds free upgrades for income-qualified households to cut gas, electricity and water use. After a home assessment, eligible homes can receive measures such as insulation, efficient furnaces, high-efficiency toilets and LED lighting at no cost.

The program has three streams: Home Upgrades (installed retrofits), RetroKits (free do-it-yourself kits delivered to the door) and multilingual Empower Me workshops. The Home Upgrades stream is currently waitlisting applications; RetroKits and workshops remain open.

For the Home Upgrades stream, the home must be a detached house, duplex or townhome built before 1998, and the applicant's name must be on the utility bill.
incentives: Home Upgrades (insulation, furnace, toilets, lighting and more): Free | RetroKit (DIY efficiency kit): Free | Empower Me workshops: Free
eligibility: Calgary resident; homeowner or renter | Household income (all members 18+) at or below: 1 person $52,884; 2 $65,836; 3 $80,938; 4 $98,269; 5 $111,456; 6 $125,703; 7+ $139,951 | Home Upgrades stream: detached house, duplex or townhome built before 1998 | Applicant's name on the utility bill | Owner-occupiers renting part of their home may qualify; rental income counts toward household income
howToApply: Apply online through homeupgradesprogram.ca/calgary | Join the waitlist for the Home Upgrades stream, or request a RetroKit | When selected, book the free home assessment; upgrades are installed at no cost
notes: Joining the waitlist does not guarantee upgrades. RetroKits and workshops are available while you wait. Edmonton and other Alberta communities do not currently have an equivalent free-upgrade program.

name: National Heat Pump Rebate
administrator: Government of Canada (announced by Environment and Climate Change Canada; delivery department not yet named)
summary: A new federal rebate announced on October 8, 2026 that will pay $2,000 toward an eligible cold-climate air-source heat pump, or up to $10,000 for households below the median income. Applications are not open yet.
description:
On October 8, 2026 the federal government announced a $2 billion, eight-year plan to retrofit one million homes. Its main measure for homeowners is the National Heat Pump Rebate, which is expected to fund up to 820,000 electric cold-climate air-source heat pumps.

Eligible homeowners can receive $2,000, and households with income below the median can receive up to $10,000. The government says both amounts can be combined with existing provincial programs.

The rebate is built for speed, especially when a furnace or boiler fails without warning. You apply through an online portal with basic personal details and the heat pump you plan to install, and approval is expected within 24 hours. After the heat pump is bought and installed, you upload your receipts and payment is approved within about five days, by direct deposit. No energy audit is needed before or after the installation, but the heat pump must be on the federal Eligible Products List, which has more than 100,000 models.

The portal is not open yet. The launch date, the median-income cut-off and the detailed eligibility rules have not been published.
amountDisplay: $2,000, or up to $10,000 for households below the median income
incentives: Cold-climate air-source heat pump (other eligible homeowners): $2,000 | Cold-climate air-source heat pump (households below median income): Up to $10,000
eligibility: Installing an eligible electric cold-climate air-source heat pump | The heat pump must be on the federal Eligible Products List | The larger rebate is for households below the median income; the income threshold has not been published | One rebate per person: a landlord who claims for a heat pump in a rental property they own cannot also claim for their own home | Designed for homeowners replacing a heating system that has broken down or is near the end of its life
howToApply: Sign up for updates on the federal 'One million home energy retrofits' page | Once the portal opens, apply online with your personal details and the heat pump model you plan to install | Wait for approval (expected within 24 hours), then buy and install the heat pump | Upload your receipts through the portal after installation | Receive payment by direct deposit (approval expected within about five days)
notes: Not open for applications yet. The government has not announced the launch date, the median-income cut-off, the department that will run the rebate, or whether heat pumps installed before launch will qualify. If you are counting on this rebate, check the official page before you buy. The same announcement included separate measures for rental and apartment buildings: a CMHC mortgage insurance product for retrofits of existing rental buildings, a Canada Infrastructure Bank retrofit initiative for multi-unit buildings, and renewed funding for deep-retrofit accelerators. The Prime Minister's October 8, 2026 release says both rebates "can be combined with existing provincial programs"; it does not mention utility or municipal programs.

name: City of Calgary Residential Clean Energy Improvement Program
administrator: City of Calgary (administered by Alberta Municipalities)
categories: financing | heat-pumps | insulation | windows-doors | solar | water-heaters
summary: Calgary's property-tax financing for home energy upgrades of up to $50,000; residential intake is closed until winter 2026/2027.
description:
Calgary's residential CEIP lets homeowners finance up to 100% of eligible energy efficiency and renewable energy upgrades, to a maximum of $50,000, and repay over up to 20 years on their property tax bill. Early repayment is allowed without penalty.

The City estimates the interest rate for the next intake at about 6.00% to 6.10%; the exact range is posted about a week before applications open and the rate is fixed for your loan. It is a loan, not a rebate: all borrowed money is repaid.

The City's page says residential CEIP is closed until winter 2026/2027. Residents can sign up for email notice of the reopening.
incentives: Eligible efficiency and renewable upgrades: Up to $50,000 (100% of costs)
eligibility: Owner listed on the Certificate of Title of a low-rise residential property in Calgary (detached or semi-detached house, row house, townhome, or qualifying residential part of a mixed-use or multi-unit building); new builds do not qualify | No property tax arrears or foreclosure, and other financial requirements on the City's page | Upgrades from the CEIP eligible list, installed by a CEIP-qualified contractor; no DIY work | Application approved before any work starts | Upgrades completed by November 15 are added to the next year's tax bill
howToApply: Sign up for City of Calgary CEIP email updates to hear when intake reopens | When open, submit the pre-qualification form through Alberta Municipalities at ceip.abmunis.ca | Get an EnerGuide evaluation, choose a qualified contractor and submit the project application | Sign the agreements, complete the work and a post-project EnerGuide evaluation, then repay through property taxes starting the following June 30
notes: No exact reopening date has been published. Projects started before approval cannot be financed, so wait for approval before signing a contract. Income-qualified Calgarians can also apply to the free Calgary Home Upgrades Program.

name: Canada Greener Homes Loan
administrator: Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (with Natural Resources Canada)
categories: financing | heat-pumps | insulation | windows-doors | air-sealing | solar | water-heaters | heating-systems
summary: An interest-free loan of $5,000 to $40,000 for energy retrofits that closed to new applicants on October 1, 2025. Homeowners already approved can still finish their projects.
description:
The Canada Greener Homes Loan offered homeowners an unsecured, interest-free loan of between $5,000 and $40,000, repayable over 10 years, to pay for retrofits recommended in an EnerGuide evaluation. Part of the loan could be advanced upfront to cover contractor deposits.

The last day to apply was October 1, 2025, and the program is now closed to new applicants. Borrowers who were already approved may continue their retrofits and submit funding requests through the loan portal.

There is currently no federal replacement loan for individual homeowners. Many provinces and municipalities run their own low- or zero-interest retrofit loans.
incentives: Interest-free retrofit loan, 10-year term: $5,000 to $40,000
eligibility: Closed to new applicants since October 1, 2025 | Previously approved borrowers can continue their projects
howToApply: New applications are not accepted | Existing borrowers: log in to the loan portal to submit post-retrofit results and funding requests
notes: Closed to new applicants: October 1, 2025 was the last day to apply, and CMHC closed the application portal on October 2, 2025. If you already have an approved loan, your funding remains available and you can keep submitting funding requests through the loan portal (questions: 1-866-292-9517 or Questions@cghli.ca). There is no federal replacement loan for individual homeowners. In Ontario, look at municipal loans such as Toronto's Home Energy Loan Program, the Better Homes Ottawa Loan Program or the Durham Greener Homes Loan.

name: Oil to Heat Pump Affordability Program
administrator: Natural Resources Canada (transitioning to Environment and Climate Change Canada), with provincial/territorial co-delivery partners
summary: Upfront grants for lower-income homeowners switching from oil heating to a heat pump. Where Ottawa delivered the program alone, the last day to apply was July 31, 2026; approved applicants have until January 31, 2027 to finish the work and submit paperwork.
description:
The Oil to Heat Pump Affordability program helps households with median or lower after-tax income replace oil heating with an electric heat pump. Approved homeowners receive the money upfront, before installation, so they do not have to carry the cost.

Where the federal government delivers the program alone (Alberta, Manitoba, Northwest Territories, Quebec and Saskatchewan), the grant is up to $10,000. In provinces and territories that co-deliver it (British Columbia, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, Ontario, Prince Edward Island and Yukon), combined support can reach up to $25,000, plus a one-time $250 payment, with rules that vary by province. In Ontario it is offered as a free heat pump installation worth up to $25,000 through Save on Energy's Energy Affordability Program.

For the federally delivered provinces and territories, the last day to apply was July 31, 2026. Applications sent by then are still being processed, and approved participants must complete and pay for the work and upload final receipts and the contractor attestation by January 31, 2027. In co-delivery provinces, intake is set by the provincial partner.
amountDisplay: Up to $10,000 federal; up to $25,000 in some co-delivered provinces (closed to new applicants)
incentives: Oil-to-heat-pump switch (federally delivered: AB, MB, NT, QC, SK): Up to $10,000 | Oil-to-heat-pump switch (co-delivered provinces/territories): Up to $25,000 | One-time bonus payment (co-delivered jurisdictions): $250
eligibility: Owner-occupant whose primary residence is heated with oil | Household after-tax income at or below the regional median | Home connected to an integrated electricity grid (Nunavut and remote off-grid communities excluded) | Homeowner had to apply personally; contractors could not apply on their behalf
howToApply: Federally delivered provinces and territories: new applications closed on July 31, 2026 | Existing applicants: finish the installation and upload receipts and the attestation form in the Canada Greener Homes portal by January 31, 2027 | Co-delivery provinces and territories: check your provincial program for any remaining intake (in Ontario, the Energy Affordability Program) | Otherwise, look at the upcoming National Heat Pump Rebate and provincial heat pump rebates
notes: Closed to new federal applications. Questions now go to Environment and Climate Change Canada at enviroinfo@ec.gc.ca or 1-800-668-6767. Homeowners must apply themselves; contractors cannot apply on their behalf. If you still heat with oil, look at the upcoming National Heat Pump Rebate, the Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program where it is offered, and provincial programs such as Ontario's Energy Affordability Program and Home Renovation Savings.

name: Oil to Heat Pump Affordability Program (NB Power advance funding)
administrator: Natural Resources Canada, delivered by NB Power
summary: Advance funding of up to $15,000 to replace oil heat with a heat pump closed to new registrations on June 30, 2026; registered participants had to file paperwork by October 1, 2026 and finish by March 31, 2027.
description:
Eligible New Brunswick homeowners could receive an advance payment based on approved contractor quotes, up to $15,000, to replace oil heat with a whole-home heat pump system. The advance could also cover electrical upgrades, ground-loop piping, oil tank removal and supplemental electric heat. Natural Resources Canada also paid a one-time $250 bonus.

Registration closed June 30, 2026. Registered participants had to submit their paperwork and quotes by October 1, 2026, and all work plus the final evaluation must be complete by March 31, 2027 or the advance must be repaid. No extensions are offered.
incentives: Whole-home heat pump replacing oil: Up to $15,000 advance | NRCan bonus: $250
eligibility: Registered on or before June 30, 2026 | Primary residence heated by oil, with household income documentation reviewed by NB Power
howToApply: Closed to new registrations
notes: Alternatives: households with income of $70,000 or less can join the Enhanced Energy Savings Program waiting list for free upgrades, and households above that can claim Total Home heat pump rebates of up to $2,000. The federal government announced a National Heat Pump Rebate in October 2026; details had not been released yet.

name: Oil to Heat Pump Affordability Program (Nova Scotia delivery)
administrator: Natural Resources Canada, delivered by Efficiency Nova Scotia (EfficiencyOne)
summary: The federal program that paid most or all of the cost for moderate-income Nova Scotia households to switch from oil heat to a heat pump stopped taking new applications on July 2, 2026.
description:
OHPA covered the cost of a cold-climate ducted or ductless heat pump for oil-heated homes in Nova Scotia, with payment sent directly to the contractor after the installation close-out paperwork was submitted.

Efficiency Nova Scotia stopped accepting applications on July 2, 2026 because the Nova Scotia funding was fully allocated. Complete applications received before that date, and households on the standby list, are still reviewed if funding becomes available, but neither guarantees funding.
incentives: Heat pump replacing oil heat: Up to $15,000
eligibility: Owner-occupied primary residence in Nova Scotia | Home mainly heated by oil, using at least 500 litres in the previous 12 months (proof of purchases required) | After-tax household income at or below: 1 person $37,260; 2 people $77,050; 3 people $98,900; 4 people $120,750; 5+ people $126,500 (line 23600 minus line 43500) | Only cold-climate centrally ducted or ductless mini-split air-source heat pumps qualified
howToApply: No longer accepting applications; see alternatives in notes
notes: If you applied before July 2, 2026, follow the instructions in your welcome letter and contact Efficiency Nova Scotia before starting or changing work. Alternatives: Home Energy Assessment rebates (up to $5,000) plus the Moderate Income Rebate top-up (up to $5,000) for homes heated with non-electric fuel, and HomeWarming for lower-income homeowners, which may include a single-zone heat pump but not a whole-home system. The federal government announced a National Heat Pump Rebate in October 2026; details had not been released yet.

name: Canada Greener Homes Grant
categories: heat-pumps | insulation | windows-doors | air-sealing | energy-audits | solar | water-heaters | heating-systems
summary: The federal grant of up to $5,000 for home retrofits (plus up to $600 for EnerGuide evaluations) is fully closed. New applications stopped in February 2024 and the final payment deadline passed on December 31, 2025.
description:
The Canada Greener Homes Grant ran from May 2021 to February 2024 and reimbursed homeowners for upgrades recommended by a registered energy advisor, such as heat pumps, insulation, windows and doors, air sealing and solar panels. It paid up to $5,000 for retrofits plus up to $600 toward the before-and-after EnerGuide evaluations.

The program closed to new participants in early 2024. People already enrolled had until December 31, 2025 to finish their work and request payment, and requests after that date are not processed.

More than 400,000 households completed retrofits through the program, with heat pumps the most popular upgrade. Anyone searching for it today should look at the replacement programs listed below.
incentives: Eligible retrofits (heat pumps, insulation, windows, solar, etc.): Up to $5,000 | Pre- and post-retrofit EnerGuide evaluations: Up to $600
eligibility: Closed: no longer accepting applications or payment requests
howToApply: This program is closed and cannot be applied for | Look at the upcoming National Heat Pump Rebate, the Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program and your provincial programs instead
notes: Fully closed. The last day for enrolled participants to submit documents was December 31, 2025, and later payment requests are not processed. In Ontario the grant was delivered jointly with Enbridge's Home Efficiency Rebate Plus. Current options: the upcoming National Heat Pump Rebate, the income-tested Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program, and provincial programs such as Ontario's Home Renovation Savings.

name: Incentives for Zero-Emission Vehicles Program
summary: The original federal EV rebate of up to $5,000 was paused on January 12, 2025 when its funding ran out, and formally ended on March 31, 2025. It has been replaced by the Electric Vehicle Affordability Program.
description:
Launched in May 2019, iZEV gave buyers and lessees of eligible zero-emission vehicles a point-of-sale incentive of up to $5,000, or up to $2,500 for plug-in hybrids with less than 50 km of electric range.

Transport Canada warned on January 10, 2025 that funding was nearly used up and paused the program on January 12, 2025, after receiving more than 559,000 reimbursement requests. The program officially closed on March 31, 2025.

If you are shopping for an EV now, the replacement is the Electric Vehicle Affordability Program, which started on February 16, 2026.
incentives: Battery-electric, fuel-cell and plug-in hybrids with 50 km or more of electric range: Up to $5,000 | Plug-in hybrids with under 50 km of electric range: Up to $2,500
eligibility: Closed: no new incentives are available
howToApply: This program has ended | See the Electric Vehicle Affordability Program for the current federal EV incentive
notes: Closed. The current federal EV incentive is the Electric Vehicle Affordability Program, which started February 16, 2026. Unlike iZEV, it has a $50,000 price cap for vehicles not built in Canada and requires the vehicle to be made in Canada or a country with which Canada has a free-trade agreement.

name: Canada Secondary Suite Loan Program
summary: A proposed low-interest federal loan of up to $80,000 for adding a secondary suite. It never opened to applicants, and Budget 2025 confirmed it will not be implemented.
description:
The Canada Secondary Suite Loan Program was announced in Budget 2024, with $409.6 million for CMHC, as a low-interest loan to help homeowners add basement apartments, garden suites or laneway homes. In December 2024 the government proposed raising the maximum from $40,000 to $80,000, at a 2% rate over 15 years, with a launch planned for early 2025.

The program never opened. Budget 2025, as part of a spending review at CMHC, said it would not be implemented because it would largely overlap with the insured-mortgage changes announced in January 2025.

Many websites still describe this loan as available. Homeowners who want to build a suite can instead ask their lender about insured mortgage refinancing for secondary suites, and should check the Multigenerational Home Renovation Tax Credit if the unit is for a senior or a relative with a disability.
eligibility: Not available: the program was cancelled before launch
howToApply: No applications were ever accepted | Ask your lender about insured mortgage refinancing for a secondary suite instead | If the unit is for a senior or adult with a disability, see the Multigenerational Home Renovation Tax Credit
notes: This loan was never available. Since January 15, 2025, homeowners can refinance with an insured mortgage to pay for a secondary suite: up to 90% of the home's value after the renovation, for homes valued up to $2 million, with amortization of up to 30 years. Ask your lender whether you qualify. This is not a home energy program.

name: Oil to Heat Pump Affordability Program (PEI)
administrator: Natural Resources Canada and the Government of PEI
summary: The federal-provincial program helping income-qualified Islanders replace oil heat with heat pumps is closed to new applicants.
description:
OHPA on PEI was co-delivered by the province and Natural Resources Canada as a direct-install program: approved low- to median-income households heating with oil had a cold-climate heat pump installed at no cost. Applications went through the province's free heat pump program portal.

The program is closed to new applicants; previously approved households are still being served.
howToApply: Closed
notes: Alternatives: the Free Home Insulation Program and the federal National Heat Pump Rebate announced in October 2026 (details pending). Confirm current details with efficiencyPEI (1-877-734-6336 or efficiencypei@gov.pe.ca) before you start.

name: Zero Emission Vehicle Infrastructure Program
summary: Federal cost-share funding for EV chargers installed by organizations, including chargers in larger apartment and condo buildings. It is not open to individuals, and no intake is currently accepting applications.
description:
ZEVIP pays up to 50% of the cost of EV charging projects (75% for Indigenous organizations and communities) carried out by organizations such as businesses, utilities, non-profits, condo or property managers, and governments. Individual homeowners cannot apply.

Past calls for proposals funded chargers in multi-unit residential buildings that fall under Part 3 of the National Building Code (a common entrance and either at least three storeys or a footprint over 600 m²), with Level 2 chargers funded up to $5,000 per connector. Funding has also flowed through delivery organizations that run smaller local charger programs.

All ZEVIP streams are closed to applications, including a fast-charging corridor pilot that ran from November 2025 to March 20, 2026. Program funding runs to March 31, 2027.
amountDisplay: Up to 50% of project costs for organizations (no open intake)
incentives: Level 2 chargers in multi-unit residential buildings: Up to 50% of costs, max $5,000 per connector
eligibility: Canadian legal entities (businesses, not-for-profits, utilities, Indigenous organizations, provincial and municipal governments) | Individuals are not eligible | Multi-unit residential projects must be in Part 3 buildings under the National Building Code
howToApply: Watch the ZEVIP page for the next call for proposals | Condo boards and landlords should also check provincial and utility charger programs
notes: No ZEVIP intake is open as of October 2026. Natural Resources Canada has committed to posting the approximate timing of future calls at least three months ahead, so condo boards and property managers planning chargers should watch the program page. Private projects over $20 million are directed to the Canada Infrastructure Bank instead. There is no federal EV charger rebate for individual homeowners; check provincial and utility programs.

name: Heat Pump Rebates (Energy Efficient Equipment Rebates)
summary: PEI's heat pump rebates ended on April 15, 2026; only heat pumps bought between April 15, 2025 and April 15, 2026 can still be claimed, within one year of purchase.
description:
efficiencyPEI paid rebates on cold-climate air-source and geothermal heat pumps installed by Network of Excellence contractors, with higher amounts for income-qualified households. The province reports that these rebates, along with most other residential equipment rebates, ended on April 15, 2026.

The last published amounts were $900 for a mini-split ($1,800 income-qualified), $2,500 for a central system ($4,500 income-qualified) and $4,000 for ground-source ($7,500 income-qualified). Equipment bought between April 15, 2025 and April 15, 2026 can still be claimed within one year of purchase.
incentives: Mini-split air-source heat pump (last rate): $900 | Mini-split air-source heat pump, income-qualified (last rate): $1,800 | Central air-to-air or air-to-water heat pump (last rate): $2,500 | Central heat pump, income-qualified (last rate): $4,500 | Ground-source heat pump (last rate): $4,000 | Ground-source heat pump, income-qualified (last rate): $7,500
eligibility: Equipment purchased between April 15, 2025 and April 15, 2026 | Claim within one year of purchase
howToApply: Apply online through the province's heat pump page for eligible past purchases
notes: Businesses and farms can look at efficiencyPEI's business programs. The federal National Heat Pump Rebate announced in October 2026 may help once details are released. Confirm current details with efficiencyPEI (1-877-734-6336 or efficiencypei@gov.pe.ca) before you start.

name: Solar Electric Rebate Program
summary: PEI's residential solar rebate is not taking new applications; it was paused in 2025 when funding ran out and listed as ended or paused as of April 15, 2026 while 2026-27 funding is decided.
description:
The program paid a per-kW rebate on grid-tied solar PV. In 2025 the residential rate was halved to $500 per kW with a $5,000 cap, and the program then became fully subscribed.

As of April 2026 the province said intake remains paused while funding and final program details for 2026-27 are finalized. No reopening had been confirmed by October 2026.
incentives: Residential solar PV (last rate): $500 per kW
howToApply: Paused; watch efficiencyPEI for a 2026-27 announcement
notes: Some websites still list the program as open with older, higher amounts; those are out of date. The program may reopen once 2026-27 funding is set. Confirm current details with efficiencyPEI (1-877-734-6336 or efficiencypei@gov.pe.ca) before you start.

name: Clean Home Heating Initiative
administrator: Enbridge Gas and the Government of Ontario
regions: Ajax | Barrie | London | Peterborough | Pickering | St. Catharines | Sault Ste. Marie | Whitby
summary: A former pilot that paid up to $4,500 toward hybrid heating, an electric heat pump paired with a gas furnace, in eight Ontario cities. All funding was allocated and it closed in February 2024.
description:
The Clean Home Heating Initiative paid incentives of about $3,000 to $4,500 to homeowners in selected cities who added an air-source heat pump with smart controls to a natural gas furnace. The controls switched between fuels based on cost and efficiency.

The pilot started in 2022 and expanded in 2023. Enbridge stopped accepting participants on February 23, 2024, once all funding was allocated.
incentives: Hybrid heating system (air-source heat pump + smart controls with gas furnace): $3,000 to $4,500
eligibility: No longer accepting participants.
howToApply: Closed. Gas-heated homes can get heat pump rebates through Home Renovation Savings.
notes: Closed, and Enbridge has removed the program's web page. Homes heated by Enbridge natural gas can now get $500 per ton, up to $2,000, toward a cold-climate air-source heat pump through Home Renovation Savings, and homes heated by electricity, oil, propane or wood can get up to $7,500.

name: CleanBC Go Electric Passenger Vehicle Rebate
administrator: Province of B.C. (Ministry of Energy and Climate Solutions)
summary: B.C.'s point-of-sale rebate for new electric cars has been paused since May 15, 2025 and is not taking applications.
description:
The Go Electric passenger vehicle rebate gave B.C. buyers an income-tested discount at the dealership on new battery-electric, fuel cell and plug-in hybrid vehicles. Funding ran through May 15, 2025, after which the Province paused the program while it reviewed next steps, citing the end of federal EV rebates and wider spending pressures.

At its peak, individuals with income under $80,000 could get up to $4,000 for a battery-electric, fuel cell or long-range plug-in hybrid, or $2,000 for a short-range plug-in hybrid, with smaller amounts up to $100,000 of income.

No restart has been announced. A separate rebate for commercial vehicles bought by businesses and organizations is available again in 2026. Households can still use the federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program and BC Hydro's home charger rebate.
incentives: Battery-electric, fuel cell or long-range (85 km+) plug-in hybrid: Was up to $4,000 (paused) | Plug-in hybrid with under 85 km range: Was up to $2,000 (paused)
eligibility: Program paused; no new applications accepted
howToApply: Not currently available; check goelectricbc.gov.bc.ca for any restart
notes: Vehicles bought or leased after May 15, 2025 do not qualify. Alternatives: the federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program and BC Hydro's home EV charger rebate (up to $350).

name: Electric Vehicle Incentive
administrator: Government of Prince Edward Island (Access PEI)
summary: PEI's point-of-sale rebate on new and used EVs has been paused since April 15, 2026 while 2026-27 funding is finalized.
description:
The incentive was applied by PEI dealers at the point of sale on purchases and leases of battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles. The last rates were $4,000 for battery-electric and $2,000 for plug-in hybrids; Teslas were removed from eligibility in March 2025, and the free Level 2 charger perk was dropped in 2025.

The province says it will provide an update as soon as possible. No resumption had been announced by October 2026.
incentives: Battery-electric vehicle (last rate): $4,000 | Plug-in hybrid (last rate): $2,000
howToApply: Paused; contact EVIncentive@gov.pe.ca for updates
notes: Some guides still describe PEI's EV rebate as active; the province has paused it. For updates, email EVIncentive@gov.pe.ca. Buyers can still check the federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program.

name: Provincial EV Rebate Program
administrator: Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro on behalf of the Province
summary: Newfoundland and Labrador's rebate of $2,500 on battery-electric and $1,500 on plug-in hybrid vehicles closed to applications on March 15, 2026.
description:
The program offered rebates on new or used EVs bought from licensed dealers in the province, on a first-come, first-served basis. The application deadline was March 15, 2026.

No replacement provincial rebate has been announced. The federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program remains available.
howToApply: Closed
notes: Applications received after March 15, 2026 are not accepted. Buyers can check the federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program.

name: CoolSaver Program (Save on Energy Local Initiatives)
administrator: Independent Electricity System Operator (Save on Energy)
summary: CoolSaver offered a free central air conditioner or heat pump tune-up and $1,000 off an 18 SEER central air conditioner in parts of Toronto, York Region and Ottawa. The 2025 program closed: work orders had to be signed by October 31, 2025 and installed by December 31, 2025.
description:
CoolSaver was a Save on Energy local initiative run by the IESO for single-family homes (detached, semi-detached, row houses and townhouses) in targeted postal code areas of Toronto, York Region and Ottawa. Homeowners and tenants could get a free tune-up of a central air conditioner or central heat pump (a $250 value), a $100 discount on a refrigerant top-up during the tune-up, and $1,000 off replacing a central air conditioner rated 14 SEER or lower with one rated 18 SEER or higher. A CoolSaver contractor (Trade Ally) applied the discount on the invoice.

The 2025 program required a signed participant agreement and work order by October 31, 2025 and installation by December 31, 2025. Save on Energy no longer lists CoolSaver, and no 2026 offer has been posted.
amountDisplay: Program ended (was $1,000 off an 18 SEER central AC, plus a free tune-up)

For a new central air conditioner, consider a cold-climate heat pump instead: it cools like an air conditioner and qualifies for the Home Renovation Savings Program rebate (pre-approval needed before installing). Toronto homeowners can finance either through the Home Energy Loan Program.

name: AEA Electric Vehicle and Charger Rebate
administrator: Arctic Energy Alliance (funded by the Government of the Northwest Territories)
summary: Arctic Energy Alliance's rebate for electric vehicles and Level 2 chargers in hydro-powered NWT communities is no longer offered.
description:
From 2020, AEA offered $5,000 toward new battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles and $500 toward Level 2 chargers for residents of hydro-connected communities, with pre-approval required. The EV rebate no longer appears among AEA's current rebates and services.

The federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program remains available for new EVs.
howToApply: Not currently available; contact AEA (867-920-3333) to ask about any future offer
notes: For a new EV, the federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program discount is applied by the dealer. An automated vehicle plug-in controller for block heaters can still get a rebate through AEA's Energy-Efficient Products program.

name: Chauffez vert – Oil and Propane Heating Replacement
administrator: Government of Québec (Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs)
summary: This former grant for replacing oil or propane heating with electric systems ended on March 31, 2026.
description:
Chauffez vert paid homeowners to remove an oil or propane furnace or boiler and install a new electric or renewable heating system. The amount depended on the housing type and the fuel being replaced.

The government announced in July 2025 that the program would end. Work had to be finished and applications received by March 31, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Applicants with incomplete files, or who still had to provide their social insurance number, had until June 30, 2026. Since December 31, 2023, Québec has banned installing new oil heating appliances, including replacing one oil appliance with another.
eligibility: Program closed. No applications accepted after March 31, 2026.
howToApply: No longer accepting applications. See the alternatives in the notes.
notes: Closed on March 31, 2026, and the final document deadline of June 30, 2026 has also passed. If you still heat with oil or propane, look at LogisVert's heat pump, geothermal and electric thermal storage grants, the free heat pump for modest-income households when registration reopens, Laval's oil heating replacement subsidy if you live in Laval, and RebateHub's federal listings.

name: Éconologis
administrator: Government of Québec (Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs)
summary: A free seasonal service for modest-income households: an advisor visits the home, gives energy-saving advice and does small weatherization jobs. Registration for 2026–2027 is full.
description:
Éconologis runs every year from October 1 to March 31. An energy-efficiency advisor from Expertbâtiment Services-Conseils, the program's only authorized organization, visits the home of an eligible modest-income household, owner or tenant, whatever the heating fuel. The visit includes personalized advice on heating, hot water, appliances and lighting, plus free minor work where needed, such as caulking windows, draft-stopping doors, insulating outlets on exterior walls, and installing low-flow showerheads and faucet aerators.

The visit is also the required first step for Hydro-Québec's free heat pump offer. Demand for that offer filled the program's capacity, so registration for 2026–2027 closed early. Households that already sent in a form will be contacted to confirm eligibility and book a visit.

Questions: 1-866-266-0008, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.

name: Free Heat Pump Program
summary: PEI's program offering free heat pumps to income-qualified households is closed to new applicants; households already approved are still waiting for installations.
description:
The province and federal government have funded around 45,000 heat pump installations on PEI since 2018. New intake for free heat pumps (and the free hot water heater offer) was paused in June 2025 and remains closed.

The province says many households are still in the queue and contractors will contact them as installations proceed.
howToApply: Closed to new applicants
notes: The 2026 federal-provincial funding on PEI went to free insulation, not free heat pumps. Households already approved will be contacted by their contractor. Alternatives: the Free Home Insulation Program and, once launched, the federal National Heat Pump Rebate. Confirm current details with efficiencyPEI (1-877-734-6336 or efficiencypei@gov.pe.ca) before you start.

name: Good Energy Zero-Emission Vehicle, E-Bike and Charger Rebates
administrator: Government of Yukon, Energy Branch (Energy, Mines and Resources)
summary: Yukon's rebates on electric vehicles, e-bikes and EV chargers ended for purchases after March 31, 2026; earlier purchases can still be claimed within one year of purchase.
description:
The Government of Yukon ended its electric transportation rebates on March 31, 2026 to reduce pressure on the electricity grid. The retired rebates covered new electric vehicles, EV chargers, shipping costs for used EVs, e-bikes and electric cargo bikes, and other electric transportation devices. About $946,000 was moved to the new Dependable Grid Program.

Vehicles, bikes and chargers bought on or before March 31, 2026 remain eligible if the application reaches the Energy Branch within one year of the purchase date. The federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program still applies to new EVs.
eligibility: Only purchases made on or before March 31, 2026, claimed within one year of purchase
howToApply: Closed to new purchases; claims for earlier purchases go to the Energy Branch within one year
notes: For a new EV, the federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program discount is applied by the dealer at purchase.

name: Home Heating System Rebates
summary: Efficiency Nova Scotia's stand-alone rebates for heating equipment, which did not need a home energy assessment, ended on December 31, 2025.
description:
This program offered rebates on heat pumps and other heating equipment without an energy assessment. It closed to applications on December 31, 2025.

Efficiency Nova Scotia now offers larger, more comprehensive rebates through the Home Energy Assessment and Moderate Income Rebate programs. Its Eco Shift demand-response program has also been paused to new enrolments since April 9, 2026.
howToApply: Program closed; use the Home Energy Assessment program instead
notes: Alternatives: the Home Energy Assessment program (up to $5,000), the Moderate Income Rebate for moderate-income homes heated with non-electric fuel, HomeWarming for lower-income homeowners, and the $800 instant rebate on heat pump water heaters.

name: Nova Scotia Electric Vehicle Rebate
summary: Nova Scotia's provincial rebates for new and used electric vehicles and e-bikes have ended, and since October 1, 2026 the province charges a registration levy on EVs and plug-in hybrids.
description:
The province's point-of-sale rebates for electric cars and e-bikes are now listed by the province as past programs. A separate rebate for medium- and heavy-duty zero-emission vehicles, open only to businesses, non-profits, municipalities and First Nations, stopped taking eligibility forms on April 15, 2026.

From October 1, 2026, owners pay a levy every two years when they issue or renew a vehicle permit: $500 for battery-electric vehicles and $250 for plug-in hybrids registered at 5,000 kg or less. Regular hybrids are not charged.
howToApply: Closed
notes: The province confirms the light-duty and e-bike rebates have ended but does not publish an end date; April 4, 2025 is the date widely reported when they closed. Some vehicles and Status Card holders may be exempt from the new levy. Buyers can still check the federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program.

name: Plug-In NB Electric Vehicle Rebate
administrator: NB Power on behalf of the Province of New Brunswick
summary: New Brunswick's provincial rebates for electric vehicles and home Level 2 chargers ended June 30, 2025; vehicles bought after that date do not qualify.
description:
Plug-In NB offered rebates on new and used electric vehicles bought from dealers, plus a home charger rebate of 50% of purchase and installation cost, up to $750, for EV buyers.

The program closed June 30, 2025 and will not be extended. Buyers had 30 days after that date to submit claims. The federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program remains available.
howToApply: Closed
notes: Plug-In NB charging rebates for businesses were a separate NB Power program. Individual buyers can check the federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program.

name: SolarHomes
administrator: Efficiency Nova Scotia (EfficiencyOne) on behalf of the Province of Nova Scotia
summary: Nova Scotia's residential solar PV rebate stopped taking homeowner applications on April 17, 2025, and approved projects had to be finished by March 31, 2026.
description:
SolarHomes rebated part of the cost of grid-tied solar panels for homeowners. Demand exhausted the funding in spring 2025; applications were first come, first served, with later submissions waitlisted.

Efficiency Nova Scotia still runs a solar rebate pilot for registered non-profits and charities, but there is no current provincial solar rebate for homeowners.
howToApply: Closed to homeowners
notes: Halifax property owners can still finance solar through the municipality's Solar City program. Registered non-profits and charities can apply to the Solar for Non-Profit Organizations pilot, which pays $0.60 per watt (DC), up to 25% of pre-tax system cost and a $15,000 maximum; the installer applies on the organization's behalf.

name: Sarnia Saves
summary: A Sarnia-area pilot that offered up to $15,000 in free insulation, draft-proofing and other upgrades through approved contractors. It reached capacity and closed to new applications in spring 2026, though a smart-thermostat enrolment reward is still offered locally.
description:
Sarnia Saves was a limited-time Enbridge Gas pilot for homes with eligible postal codes in Sarnia, Point Edward and Brights Grove. Approved contractors delivered up to $15,000 in assessments, insulation, draft-proofing and other upgrades.

Enbridge says the offer reached capacity and intake is closed. Applications received by April 17, 2026 will be processed while funding lasts, and homeowners are directed to Home Renovation Savings. A separate offer still pays local residents a $75 virtual prepaid Mastercard for enrolling a smart thermostat, and another $20 for staying enrolled through brief winter adjustments from December 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.

The smart thermostat reward remains open locally.

name: Home Efficiency Retrofit Rebate
summary: Saskatchewan's utility rebate for insulation, windows, doors and air sealing ended in April 2026.
description:
HERR helped Saskatchewan homeowners improve their building envelope with high-performance windows, doors, insulation and air sealing. It was paired with the federal Canada Greener Homes Grant and required pre- and post-retrofit EnerGuide evaluations.

The program offered up to $1,800 for upgrades plus $200 toward the EnerGuide evaluations. It ended in April 2026.

There is currently no provincial or utility rebate for insulation or windows in Saskatchewan.

summary: Seasonal in-store discounts on smart thermostats, washers, dishwashers and other efficiency products; the 2026 round ended July 27, 2026.

SaskPower and SaskEnergy run periodic point-of-sale campaigns that take money off energy-efficient products at participating Saskatchewan retailers. The 2026 round ran from May 4 to July 27, 2026, and has ended.

The 2026 discounts included $75 off an ENERGY STAR smart thermostat, $100 off an ENERGY STAR clothes washer, $50 off an ENERGY STAR dishwasher and $15 off ENERGY STAR ventilation fans, with some air sealing, insulation and lighting products also included.

Earlier rounds ran in 2023 and 2024. No new round has been announced.
