HER+ was a joint Enbridge Gas and Canada Greener Homes Grant offer that paid rebates after pre- and post-retrofit energy assessments. It covered insulation, air sealing, windows and doors, heat pumps and heat pump water heaters, smart thermostats and solar, and Enbridge says it helped more than 100,000 Ontario households.

HER+ closed to new applicants on February 5, 2024. Participants had to finish their post-retrofit assessment by December 1, 2025 and have all paperwork submitted by December 31, 2025. Enbridge's separate Home Efficiency Rebate (HER) stopped taking new participants on January 27, 2025, when the Home Renovation Savings Program replaced it.

name: LogisVert – No-Cost Heat Pump for Modest-Income Households
administrator: Hydro-Québec (with Éconologis, Government of Québec and Government of Canada)
summary: Modest-income households heated by electric baseboards can get a ductless wall-mounted heat pump installed for free. Registration for the 2026–2027 season is closed.
description:
Through LogisVert, Hydro-Québec supplies and installs a free ENERGY STAR Cold Climate wall-mounted heat pump for eligible modest-income owner-occupants and tenants. Households must first get an Éconologis advisor visit, which screens them for eligibility and passes the file to Hydro-Québec. Homes that can't take a heat pump may get a free smart thermostat instead.

Registration for the 2026–2027 season has closed because demand filled the available places, and applications already received are being processed. Households visited between October 2025 and March 2026 can expect installation between summer 2026 and spring 2027; those visited between October 2026 and March 2027 can expect it from fall 2027. Authorized installers serve Montréal, Laval, Capitale-Nationale, Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean, Chaudière-Appalaches, Bas-Saint-Laurent, Montérégie, Mauricie, Côte-Nord and Gaspésie–Îles-de-la-Madeleine.

On June 29, 2026, Québec and Hydro-Québec announced more than $243 million, including $172.5 million from the federal Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program, to provide free turnkey upgrades to 20,000 low-income households. Heat pumps come first, with doors, windows and smart thermostats planned from 2027.

Solar PV was an eligible upgrade in the Total Home Energy Savings Program at $200 per kW, provided the system met NB Power's net metering requirements.

Only homeowners who enrolled by May 27, 2026 qualify, and their installation and final home energy evaluation must be completed by January 31, 2027.

name: Better Homes Kingston
categories: financing | insulation | air-sealing | windows-doors | heat-pumps | water-heaters | smart-thermostats | solar | batteries | ev-chargers | energy-audits
summary: Kingston's property-tax retrofit loan of up to $50,000, plus rebates for Utilities Kingston natural gas customers, came back in 2026 but is no longer taking applications. You can join the City's waitlist to hear about the next round.
description:
Better Homes Kingston is the City of Kingston's home energy retrofit financing program, supported by the Federation of Canadian Municipalities' Green Municipal Fund. The 2026 relaunch offered fixed-rate loans of up to $50,000 or 20% of the home's value, whichever is less. Rates were 3.25% for 5 years, 4.00% for 10, 4.50% for 15 and 4.75% for 20, repaid as a local improvement charge on the property tax bill. Up to half of the funding could be paid out up front to cover contractors, and the loan could be repaid early with no penalty.

The relaunch also added rebates for Utilities Kingston natural gas customers, available on their own or with a loan. These included up to $3,600 for exterior wall insulation, up to $1,500 for attic insulation, $500 per ton (up to $2,000) for a cold-climate air-source heat pump, $3,000 for a ground-source heat pump and $600 toward a home energy assessment.

Eligible work covered insulation, air sealing, windows and doors, heat pumps, water heaters, solar, batteries, EV chargers, electrical upgrades needed for the energy work, and flood-resilience measures such as backwater valves and sump pumps. The City now says the program is no longer accepting applications.

summary: Clean Energy Financing, which let homeowners in 12 Nova Scotia municipalities repay energy upgrades through their property tax bill, is no longer accepting new applications.

Clean Energy Financing was a property-assessed clean energy (PACE) program run by Clean Foundation with partner municipalities. The municipality paid for upgrades such as heat pumps, insulation and solar, and the homeowner repaid the cost through a charge on the property tax account.

Clean Foundation now says the program is no longer accepting new applications. Homeowners with an existing application can still contact the program team.

Terms were set by each municipality. In Bridgewater, for example, financing ran up to 15 years at a fixed 1% rate, up to $15,000 for homes assessed at $100,000 or less and otherwise the lesser of $40,000 or 15% of assessed value.

name: Switch Charlottetown
administrator: City of Charlottetown (delivered by Switch PACE)
categories: financing | heat-pumps | solar | insulation | air-sealing | windows-doors | water-heaters | smart-thermostats
summary: Charlottetown's 0% property-linked financing for heat pumps, solar, insulation and other upgrades is fully subscribed and no longer accepting new projects.
description:
Switch Charlottetown let homeowners finance energy upgrades through their property rather than personal credit, at 0% interest over 15 years. Homeowners could borrow up to $40,000 or 15% of the property's value, whichever was less, for heat pumps, geothermal, heat pump water heaters, solar, insulation and air sealing, windows, doors and smart thermostats. A 5% administration fee covered energy advice, free pre- and post-project home energy assessments and help with provincial and federal rebates.

Lower-income households (net household income of $55,000 or less and an assessed value of $300,000 or less) had the admin fee waived and could get up to $1,500 back on insulation upgrades.

The program launched in July 2021 and was fully subscribed by January 2024, with 743 projects completed or under way. The City announced the end of the first funding round in August 2024, and the program is no longer accepting new projects.

name: Better Homes Hamilton Pilot Program
summary: Hamilton's pilot offered 0% loans of up to $20,000 for insulation, air sealing and heat pumps, repaid through property taxes. It closed to applications on February 1, 2024.
description:
Better Homes Hamilton was a pilot that offered interest-free loans of up to $20,000 per home, repaid as a special charge on the property tax bill over 10 or 15 years, with an optional 30% advance to pay contractors. It focused on switching homes from gas, oil or propane to electric heating, with work such as insulation, air sealing and cold-climate heat pumps.

The pilot aimed to fund about 50 homes, with up to $1 million in total. Applications opened December 1, 2023 and closed February 1, 2024, and all applicants have been told the outcome. No new intake has been announced.
incentives: Zero-interest retrofit loan: Up to $20,000

name: Saanich Heat Pump Financing Program
administrator: District of Saanich (administered by City Green Solutions)
summary: Zero-interest financing of up to $12,000, repaid on your property taxes over 10 years, for Saanich homes replacing oil, gas or propane heat with an electric heat pump.
description:
The District of Saanich lends homeowners up to $12,000 at 0% interest to replace an oil, natural gas or propane furnace or boiler with an efficient electric heat pump. The loan is repaid over 10 years through an extra charge on your property taxes.

Ducted, ductless mini-split, air-to-water and combined space and water heat pumps qualify, and the financing can also cover related electrical service upgrades, ducting changes, duct cleaning and air filtration. The heat pump must become the home's main heat source with no fossil-fuel backup, and oil-heated homes must remove the oil equipment and tank.

The program runs in intakes, and half of the spaces each year are reserved for income-qualified households. Income-qualified participants are encouraged to register for the CleanBC Energy Savings Program first, so its rebate goes to the contractor and Saanich financing covers the rest.

Participants may also qualify for a grant toward a professional energy evaluation, and the free Home Energy Navigator can help with planning. name: Better Homes Burlington Zero-Interest Heat Pump Loan
summary: Burlington offered a limited number of zero-interest loans of up to $10,000 to help homeowners switch from gas or oil heating to an air-source heat pump. The loan has ended, but the City's free Better Homes Burlington concierge service continues.
description:
Better Homes Burlington started in 2023 as a City of Burlington pilot under the community Climate Action Plan. It offered zero-interest loans of up to $10,000 for the purchase and installation of an air-source heat pump, with up to 20 loans in the first round. Council approved a second round in 2024, with applications accepted until the end of December 2024 or until the program was full.

To qualify, the home had to be a detached, semi-detached or townhouse in Burlington, heated with gas or oil, with a City property tax account in good standing for the past five years. All owners had to consent, and owners had to enrol in the City's pre-authorized property tax payment plan.

The City has said the zero-interest loan has come to an end. Its Better Homes Burlington concierge service still helps residents find home energy rebates, incentives and resources.

name: HAT Smart Existing Homes Incentive Program
summary: Medicine Hat's 2026 rebate of up to $5,000 for insulation, windows, doors, tankless water heaters, HRV/ERV and solar is fully subscribed and no longer taking new requests.
description:
HAT Smart offers rebates to City of Medicine Hat utility customers. The 2026 Existing Homes incentive pays up to $5,000 per home for upgrades recommended in an EnerGuide evaluation, including insulation, windows, doors, tankless water heaters, heat or energy recovery ventilators and solar panels.

For 2026 the program requires both a pre- and post-renovation EnerGuide evaluation, and work must be done by a licensed installer with a City business licence. As of September 29, 2026 the program is fully subscribed and no longer accepting requests for the funding queue.

Other 2026 HAT Smart streams include a $250 utility credit for EnerGuide evaluations, a new-home incentive of up to $10,000, water conservation rebates and a scratch-and-win offer for small energy-saving items. The 2026 program year ends December 15, 2026.

name: City of Vancouver Heat Pump Top-Up
summary: Vancouver's extra rebate for single-family homes and duplexes switching from gas, oil or propane to an electric heat pump has ended.
description:
From 2018 the City of Vancouver added a top-up, most recently up to $4,000, to provincial heat pump rebates for single-family homes and duplexes that replaced fossil-fuel heating with an all-electric air source heat pump.

In 2023 the City ended the single-family heat pump top-up, made a final payment to cover applications already in the queue, and shifted its incentives toward multi-family buildings. The City does not process heat pump rebate applications itself and refers homeowners to a CleanBC Better Homes Energy Coach.

notes: The City of Vancouver no longer offers its own heat pump top-up and says it does not administer heat pump rebate applications; it refers residents to CleanBC Better Homes energy coaches. Vancouver homeowners switching from gas can look at the income-tested CleanBC Energy Savings Program or the upcoming federal National Heat Pump Rebate. Electric-heated homes can use the Home Renovation Rebate Program, though Vancouver homes cannot claim its Tier 2 window and door rebate. Heat pump installs in Vancouver need a mechanical permit.

name: Edmonton Change Homes for Climate Solar Program
summary: Edmonton's solar panel rebates for single-family and multi-unit properties are fully subscribed and no longer accepting applications.
description:
The City of Edmonton has run several rounds of rooftop solar rebates. The most recent round opened on March 17, 2025 for multi-unit residential properties with four or more dwellings, paying $0.50 per watt up to $4,000 per dwelling from a budget of up to $2.3 million. Its full budget was committed by August 18, 2025, and installations had to be completed by November 3, 2025.

The City states that its residential solar rebate, for both single-family and multi-unit properties, is fully subscribed. Solar remains eligible for financing through Edmonton's CEIP.

The District of West Vancouver added its own top-ups to the CleanBC Better Homes rebates for homes switching from gas, oil, wood or propane to electric: $1,500 toward an electrical service upgrade and $1,000 toward a heat pump water heater. Eligibility was assessed automatically through the CleanBC Better Homes program.

When the Province ended Better Homes fuel-switching rebates on April 11, 2025, the District's top-ups ended too. Work completed, or quotes received, before that date may still qualify through the Better Homes program.

name: Canmore Residential Solar Incentive
summary: Canmore's 2026 lottery for twenty $1,250 rooftop solar incentives is closed. The Town expects to offer the incentive again in 2027.
description:
The Town of Canmore offers a yearly incentive for homeowners who install rooftop solar PV. For 2026 it funded 20 incentives of $1,250 each, for new systems of at least 3 kW on single-family homes, duplexes, tri- and four-plexes and individual townhouses.

If more people apply than there is funding, the Town picks recipients by lottery. Systems already installed don't qualify, and selected projects must finish installation and electrical inspection by December 15.

Applications for 2026 are closed. The Town says to check back for the 2027 round.

name: City of Lethbridge Clean Energy Improvement Program

summary: Lethbridge’s property-tax financing covers up to 100% of home energy upgrades at a fixed 2.83% over up to 25 years, with a $1,350 rebate on completed projects. The program is at capacity and isn’t taking new pre-qualifications.
description:
The City of Lethbridge’s Clean Energy Improvement Program (CEIP) lends homeowners up to the full cost of eligible energy efficiency and renewable energy upgrades. Repayments are added to the property tax bill at a fixed 2.83% over up to 25 years, stay with the property if it is sold, and can be paid off early without penalty.

For a limited time, completed projects receive a $1,350 rebate that reduces the amount financed. Only one rebate is available per project.

The City says the program is currently at capacity and has stopped accepting new pre-qualification submissions. Applications already on the waitlist are processed in order as space opens.

description:
The City of St. Albert’s Clean Energy Improvement Program (CEIP) finances up to the full cost of eligible energy upgrades, repaid on the property tax bill. Completed projects receive a $1,400 incentive applied to the Clean Energy Improvement Tax, which lowers the amount financed. Incentives are limited, first come, first served, and one per project.

The program reached capacity and closed pre-qualification submissions on October 1, 2026. Submissions already on the waitlist are processed as space becomes available.
